" alt= " The Gee-Gees will monitor guard Calvin Epistola , who has been nursing an ankle injury , carefully . " data-portal-copyright= " Wayne Cuddington " **28;15216;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 567362 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Carleton Ravens and Dalhousie Tigers men&amp;rsquo ; s basketball teams have each lost only one of more than 30 games this season , both by a single point . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This matters in the context of the Canadian university men&amp;rsquo ; s basketball championship because the University of Ottawa Gee-Gees , the only team to beat the Ravens on Feb. 7 , are the Tigers&amp;rsquo ; opponents for an opening-round game at TD Place arena on Friday night . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Perhaps it was mere coincidence , but the Gee-Gees&amp;rsquo ; 68-67 triumph against the Ravens , also at TD Place , produced the second-lowest combined score of any Ravens game all season . The lowest was a 69-65 Carleton victory against Ottawa at the Ravens&amp;rsquo ; Nest in December . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Here&amp;rsquo ; s something else to consider : The Tigers&amp;rsquo ; 78-77 setback against the host St. Francis Xavier X-Men in January featured the lowest winning-team score for any Dalhousie contest in 2019-20. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; All that suggests the best option for the Gee-Gees and five other teams intent on toppling the top-seeded Ravens and No. 2-ranked Tigers for the W.P. McGee Trophy would be to slow the pace and reduce the number of scoring opportunities . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;15246;TOOLONG ... title= " Gee-Gees coach James Derouin said it 's often all about defence when two strong teams meet . " alt= " Gee-Gees coach James Derouin said it 's often all about defence when two strong teams meet . " data-portal-copyright= " Wayne Cuddington " **28;15282;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 567361 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; When you put two good teams together , especially in basketball , a lot of times that&amp;rsquo ; s the way it ends up , &amp;rdquo ; Gee-Gees head coach James Derouin said . &amp;ldquo ; If you look at the history of the tournament , when two really good teams match up , often the game is in the 60s and 70s. &amp;hellip ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Some of it is the pace , but a lot of it is really , really good defence and a tougher ( arena ) environment in order to score . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Fifth-year guard Calvin Epistola said the Gee-Gees won the Capital Hoops Classic because they remained true to themselves . &amp;ldquo ; We were successful against Carleton with that game plan , and also against Ryerson in the ( Ontario conference ) quarterfinals . If we stick to what we know and are good at , then we&amp;rsquo ; ll be fine . We have to compete , defend and rebound . It&amp;rsquo ; s that simple . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It bears repeating that neither Dalhousie nor Carleton has lost since . The Tigers are on a 12-game winning streak , including Sunday&amp;rsquo ; s 78-64 victory against St. FX in the Atlantic final , while the Ravens have taken five in a row by stunning margins : 54 against McMaster ; 63 against Brock ; 44 again against McMaster ; 35 against Ottawa in a conference semifinal ; and 22 against Western in the final . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;15312;TOOLONG ... title= " Ravens head coach Taffe Charles says losing -- unfortunately -- is a good way to learn a lot . " alt= " Ravens head coach Taffe Charles says losing -- unfortunately -- is a good way to learn a lot . " data-portal-copyright= " Tony Caldwell " **28;15348;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 567363 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; You tend to learn more from losing than from winning , unfortunately , &amp;rdquo ; Ravens head coach Taffe Charles said after practice Wednesday . &amp;ldquo ; I think we saw it coming as a coaching staff in terms of some of the things we weren&amp;rsquo ; t doing well . All ( the loss ) did was kind of reiterate some of those things . We weren&amp;rsquo ; t precise in terms of our spacing , we weren&amp;rsquo ; t precise in terms of what our plan was as a group . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There are caveats against drawing hard conclusions from earlier matchups . For example , Carleton won by 17 against its first-round opponent , the Calgary Dinos , but that was in early October in Victoria . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Meanwhile , the Gee-Gees played the Feb. 26 playoff semifinal at the Ravens&amp;rsquo ; Nest without Epistola , who injured his left ankle four days earlier against the Ryerson Rams , and another fifth-year guard , Sean Stoqua , also sat out because of a tender ankle . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Derouin said it was a tough choice because those Gee-Gees , in their final years of eligibility , would never have another chance to win an Ontario University Athletics title . Given the state of Epistola&amp;rsquo ; s ankle in particular and the guaranteed host-team spot in the Final 8 , however , it was clearly the best choice , not that it felt like that immediately after the Ravens won 96-61. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I couldn&amp;rsquo ; t wait to get to the car and get out of there , &amp;rdquo ; Derouin said . &amp;ldquo ; Now it seems like an obvious one , now it seems like a no-brainer , but , in that moment , with the competitive juices , this rivalry , you don&amp;rsquo ; t want ever to just punt one &amp;hellip ; but I can admit it was still super hard to do . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A week later , Epistola has remained on limited minutes during practices and , with the possibility of as many as three games in three days , Derouin will monitor him carefully . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Besides , dwelling on a sore ankle or two won&amp;rsquo ; t help solve the puzzles awaiting the Gee-Gees , starting with those posed by the Tigers , whose roster features first-team all-Canadian guard and player of the year nominee Keevan Veinot and top defensive player nominee Xavier Ochu. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Tigers head coach Rick Plato shrugged off any potential impact from the defeat at St. FX , saying that contest capped an eight-day span involving four road games and two travel delays because of winter storms . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Whether it was one point or 20 points , we had our chances to win and just didn&amp;rsquo ; t do it . But you know what ? You learn that you can&amp;rsquo ; t take anything for granted . You can&amp;rsquo ; t base any future game on what you have done in the past , &amp;rdquo ; Plato said Wednesday . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s not going to be easy playing Ottawa in , essentially , their home den , but it&amp;rsquo ; ll be fun . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Dalhousie downed uOttawa 87-83 in the first round of the 2016 nationals at Vancouver , but then lost 76-66 to Carleton in a semifinal . Last year , in Halifax , &amp;nbsp ; the Ravens won another semifinal showdown 76-65. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Like the Gee-Gees , the Ravens will hope for home-court success against the Dinos and whoever else might subsequently stand in the way of what would be Carleton&amp;rsquo ; s 15th national championship . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s always great to have the home crowd and especially to have ( the tournament ) in your city , &amp;rdquo ; Ravens guard Munis Tutu said . &amp;ldquo ; We just have to come in and represent , and that&amp;rsquo ; s what we look forward to doing this weekend . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; gholder@postmedia.com &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : //twitter.com/HolderGord " &gt;Twit ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2&gt;Tournament game schedule&lt;/h2&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;THURSDAY , March 5&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Women 's **27;15378;TOOLONG : Ryerson Rams ( 3 ) vs . " data-portal-copyright= " Tom Braid " **28;17190;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 566926 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : //www.youtu ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; There seems to be a lot of equity in the 2020 Canadian university basketball championships in Ottawa , including equal numbers of women&amp;rsquo ; s and men&amp;rsquo ; s teams and players and essentially matching schedules . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; What stands out as unequal is a comparative disparity on the sidelines , where Lisa Thomaidis of the Saskatchewan Huskies and Carly Clarke of the Ryerson Rams constitute the entire population of female head coaches among the eight in the women&amp;rsquo ; s portion of the event and the 16 overall in the U Sports tournaments at TD Place arena and the Ravens&amp;rsquo ; Nest at Carleton University . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The numbers from across Canada tell a similar tale , with only 18 of 48 teams piloted by women during the 2019-20 season . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I have been involved in university sport for over 30 years and that statistic that you quoted has not changed , the needle has not changed , and specifically at high-performance sport , so it&amp;rsquo ; s an absolutely systemic issue , &amp;rdquo ; Jennifer Brenning , Carleton&amp;rsquo ; s assistance vice-president for recreation and athletics , said Wednesday . &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s not unique to U Sport . It&amp;rsquo ; s not unique to basketball . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I have tried to hire women over the years to coach our teams , and what we are finding is that women will not step up to those positions until they feel absolutely well qualified and with the experience . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s different for men coaches . They are coaching club basketball . They came up and they&amp;rsquo ; re willing to put in time for very little pay . It is also about work-life balance . It&amp;rsquo ; s a challenging career . You don&amp;rsquo ; t get your weekends off , you&amp;rsquo ; re working nights and days and you&amp;rsquo ; re putting lots of hours in. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There are things we have to look at to support our women coaches . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Lisette Johnson Stapley , chief sport officer for U Sport , said the national governing body recently obtained $75,000 in Sport Canada funding for a mentorship and apprenticeship program for female coaches . Its end goal is to increase the number of candidates and , eventually , the number of women as coaches . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; When we run our internal teams , whether it&amp;rsquo ; s for FISU ( World University Games ) , whether it&amp;rsquo ; s for the hockey all-stars , we find that it&amp;rsquo ; s many men and not very many women stepping up to the plate , &amp;rdquo ; Johnson Stapley said . &amp;ldquo ; Again , it&amp;rsquo ; s work-life balance , children &amp;hellip ; They can&amp;rsquo ; t afford the time . " data-portal-copyright= " JAVIER SORIANO " **28;17256;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 566928 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Now concluding her 22nd season with the Huskies , Thomaidis said it was easier for her to throw herself into the job 100 per cent at the start because she knew not a soul in Saskatoon before moving there and because the team had not enjoyed success , making any new success addictive . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In addition , where once she had to do &amp;ldquo ; everything&amp;rdquo ; herself , Thomaidis now has a full-time assistant and associate head coach and additional financial resources , so she has off-loaded some tasks . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; You&amp;rsquo ; re wired a little bit differently if you want to do this job and do it really well , &amp;rdquo ; said Thomaidis , who in addition to a 2015 national title has the Huskies on a run of 13 consecutive appearances at nationals . Her overall record is 472-269 &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; You&amp;rsquo ; re always kind of thirsty for knowledge , you&amp;rsquo ; re always trying to watch that one more game film or make that one more recruiting call . " data-portal-copyright= " Wayne Cuddington " **28;20341;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 564490 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The University of Ottawa Gee-Gees have taken another big step toward the Canadian university women&amp;rsquo ; s basketball championship , while the Carleton Ravens will just have to sit back and wait . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Gee-Gees shut down the Ravens&amp;rsquo ; offence in the fourth quarter , outscoring their rivals 19-9 in the frame on the way to a 57-48 victory in an Ontario University Athletics semifinal game at Montpetit Hall on Saturday night . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Next up for the Gee-Gees is a semifinal confrontation against the Ryerson Rams , who downed the Queen&amp;rsquo ; s Gaels 74-59 in another Saturday quarterfinal , next Wednesday at Montpetit Hall . They met once during the regular season in Toronto , with Ottawa claiming a 74-72 victory . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Besides advancing to the OUA&amp;rsquo ; s Critelli Cup final , the winners of that contest will receive one of the conference&amp;rsquo ; s two berths in the nationals , scheduled for TD Place arena on March 5-8 . The losers will have to hope their overall performance is enough to impress the committee that will award a single wild-card berth and determine the seedings for the U Sports tournament . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Ravens have long known they would be in nationals as the designated host team . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;20371;TOOLONG ... title= " Ottawa Gee Gees logo " alt= " Ottawa Gee Gees logo " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;20407;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 564438 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Meanwhile , Carleton and Ottawa will meet in the men&amp;rsquo ; s Wilson Cup semifinals after winning home-court quarterfinals on Saturday night . The Ravens thumped the McMaster Marauders 108-64 , while the Gee-Gees downed Ryerson 75-54. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The victory for the uOttawa women was their third in as many tries against Carleton this season . They also won 66-49 at the Ravens&amp;rsquo ; Nest in December and 77-75 at TD Place earlier this month . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; On Saturday , A &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;ngela Ribarich topped the Gee-Gees offensively with a game-high 18 points on 9-for-12 shooting . Brooklynn McAlear-Fanus , who played all 40 minutes , added 13 points . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Playing without leading scorer Alyssa Cerino , a fifth-year forward , the Ravens led 26-24 at halftime and 39-38 through three quarters , but ran out of fuel in the fourth . They were paced by 11 points from Madison Reid and 10 from Tatyanna Burke . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The other women&amp;rsquo ; s semifinal will feature the Brock Badgers against Western in London on Wednesday night . The Badgers rallied from 19 points down to top the Windsor Lancers 61-57 on Saturday , while the top-seeded Mustangs downed the Queen&amp;rsquo ; s Gaels 74-59. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;20437;TOOLONG ... title= " Carleton Ravens logo " alt= " Carleton Ravens logo " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;20473;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 564439 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Yasiin Joseph ( 22 ) and Alain Louis ( 21 ) led five Ravens in double figures with points against the Marauders , while Connor Gilmore led McMaster with 18 . Carleton led only 24-20 after one period , but pulled away to a 57-38 edge by halftime and cruised from there to the end of the contest . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Back at Montpetit Hall , Calvin Epistola and Guillaume P&amp;eacute ; pin both scored 18 points as the Gee-Gees built a substantial lead early and held off any possible comeback by the Rams . Tanor Ngom and Jayden Frederick both had 18 for Ryerson. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Wednesday&amp;rsquo ; s semifinal between Carleton and Ottawa will also be the third confrontation of the season between the clubs . Borowiecki stays home awaiting baby , Wolanin prepares for return to Belleville&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; Don BrennanSat , 08 Feb 2020 12:55:44 **45;21111;TOOLONG ... Sport Hall of Fame will add six inductees in Mayhttp : **37;21158;TOOLONG ... src= " https : **34;21197;TOOLONG ... title= " The Ottawa Sport Hall of Fame announced Thursday that basketball coach Dave Smart is one of the 2020 inductees. " alt= " The Ottawa Sport Hall of Fame announced Thursday that basketball coach Dave Smart is one of the 2020 inductees. " data-portal-copyright= " Jean Levac " **28;21233;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 548594 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Ottawa Sport Hall of Fame announced Thursday basketball coach Dave Smart , hockey player and official Marina Zenk , Carleton Sports Therapy founders Phil Ashcroft and Dr. Donald Johnson , martial arts legend John Therien and hockey pioneer Derek Holmes will be its 2020 inductees. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; They will be honoured at the Ottawa Sport Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony May 13 at the Brookstreet Hotel . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Each year the selection process seems to get more and more difficult , &amp;rdquo ; said Dave Best , chair of the Ottawa Sport Hall of Fame . &amp;ldquo ; Ottawa is home base for an exceptional pool of sporting achievement and excellence . This is reflected in the quality of the nominations we receive . This year&amp;rsquo ; s inductees are athletes , builders and champions all , with not only remarkable sports pedigrees , but impressive records of community service and volunteerism. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Smart coached the Carleton University Ravens men&amp;rsquo ; s basketball team from 1999-2015 and 2016-19 . Smart&amp;rsquo ; s teams won 13 national title and he won the Aberdeen Trophy as U Sport Coach of the Year nine times . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Zenk led the Seneca Sting women&amp;rsquo ; s hockey team to a provincial championship , then , following her playing career , she established herself as an excellent on-ice official &amp;ndash ; locally , nationally and internationally . She was the head referee at the first women&amp;rsquo ; s gold-medal game at 1998 Olympics in Nagano. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Johnson and Ashcroft&amp;nbsp ; founded the Carleton Sports Medicine Clinic in 1973 , building a world-class facility that has successfully treated tens of thousands of athletes and non-athletes . Dr. Johnson is a leading expert in the field of arthroscopic surgery . He was the team physician for the Winter and Summer Olympic teams in 1976 , as well as the Ottawa Rough Riders and Senators . Ashcroft was once the head physiotherapist for the New Zealand All Blacks and several professional soccer teams before moving to Canada where he has serviced countless local , national and international events in soccer , rugby and track and field , including the 1976 Olympics . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A ninth degree black belt in Jiu Jitsu , Therien has earned the title of &amp;ldquo ; Hanshi , &amp;rdquo ; which means &lt;em&gt;Leader of Leaders&lt;/em&gt; . He has coached and certified thousands of students to Black Belt status over the last 50 years . For nearly two decades , he was manager and coach to 23-time world kickboxing champion , Jean-Yves Theriault . Therien was inducted into the Canadian Martial Arts Hall of Fame in 2010 , and is currently the Executive Director of the World Kobuto Federation . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Holmes began as a player , toiling through various hockey leagues , winning championships and serving as captain of the Canadian eam in 1968 . @@51915618 <p> One familiar factor of late summer is the constant reporting of extreme weather in the United States and the Asian Pacific . Of course , it is hurricane season -- typhoon season , if you live in the Pacific Rim . Every year , a series of storms start out in the middle of the ocean and march , like rampaging armies , one after the other , toward landfall . <p> Most thunderstorm events do not develop into hurricanes , because high winds in the jet stream blow the tops off of the forming thunderclouds and do not give them a chance to form . This is the reason thunderclouds are shaped like a blacksmith 's anvil as the tops are sheared off by winds that can reach over 400 km-h in the stratosphere . In mid-ocean hurricane development , this effect is minimized . One of the most destructive , but least talked about effects of these violent weather events , is storm surge , which happens when the winds from a hurricane or typhoon blow water towards the shore . This causes the water to pile @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ land causing destructive flooding . <p> This effect can be made worse by the state of tides . The highest storm surge events happen when there is a full moon . This allows the gravitational effects of the sun and moon to be added to the extra water the storm blew in , resulting in high storm surge events . <p> The driving force for this weather is the sun . In late summer , the sun beats down on the ocean heating the water . This water starts to evaporate and take the sun 's heat into the atmosphere . As the water vapour condenses into clouds , the heat carried by the water vapour heats the air . <p> This effect creates a low pressure area in the centre of the storm and the winds start to move to the low pressure area . Because the Earth is spinning , these winds move in a spiral pattern and you get the massive , spinning storms that are so characteristic of a hurricane or typhoon . <p> As the storm heads toward the land , the low air pressure @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ to a half-metre in height over normal conditions . <p> These storm surges march relentlessly onto the land , destroying anything in their way . This is especially dangerous in low flat land , such as you find along many coasts around the world . For instance , in Florida , the average height above sea level is only about two metres . In some places , it is as low as only one metre . As it moves onto the land , the water can go a long way before it comes to points high enough to stop it . This problem only will get worse as icecaps melt and sea level gets higher . <p> Of course , this cycle can not continue when the hurricane makes landfall . The water vapour that is driving the system can not be supplied to the air because the hurricane no longer has the warm water to supply the vapour . That is why hurricanes quickly lose their power as they head onto land . <p> In the past few years , hurricanes and typhoons have become more powerful and more @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ our planet heats up . Climate change is not a simple process . Just because the planet is warming does not mean the hot days in the summer are due to global warming . The effects that we will notice first are more violent and more frequent storms . <p> With more energy available in the weather systems , we will see increasingly destructive and more frequent storms . We also may see the hurricane season extended . We could be in for a rough ride , weather-wise , in the future . <p> Tim Philp has enjoyed science since he was old enough to read . Having worked in technical fields all his life , he shares his love of science with readers weekly . He can be reached by e-mail at : tphilp@bfree.on.ca or via snail mail c/o The Expositor. 
@@51915626 <p> It is encouraging to see that Erin O'Toole 's leadership website has a well-presented climate change plan , decorated with the requisite frozen ocean scene . It includes a six-point " approach , " seven policy criteria and six priorities to " contribute meaningfully to lowering global GHG emissions . " The six priorities are : <p> Exporting modern and safe nuclear technology ; <p> Helping the world stop burning coal by transitioning to natural gas ; <p> Tapping the ingenuity of our scientists and researchers to develop technology that will help the world ; <p> Working with industry on a plan to get to net zero emissions in the oil and gas industry ; <p> Building climate resilience into our infrastructure ; <p> Promoting Canada as an ESG Global Energy Thought Leader . <p> Although understandably short on detail , as the newly minted Conservative leader , it is worth examining the approach , criteria and priorities O'Toole has articulated to see what may be gleaned from the language . " <p> I agree with this statement , although perhaps for different reasons . While a carbon tax does not solve all environmental problems , it is a smart way to reduce carbon-related greenhouse gas emissions , and is most certainly the policy tool most recommended by economists and business leaders in Canada , including many of Canada 's largest oil producers . <p> A carbon tax is not sufficient for addressing many greenhouse gases ( methane , nitrogen oxides ) , nor even the majority of carbon-related greenhouse gases . It is an important part of the climate policy mix , but not the economy-bashing bogeyman the Conservatives portray it to be , nor the climate panacea touted by economists . @@51915738 <h> How Plants Close the Door on Infection <p> Plants have a unique ability to safeguard themselves against pathogens by closing their pores -- but until now , no one knew quite how they did it . Scientists have known that a flood of calcium into the cells surrounding the pores triggers them to close , but how the calcium entered the cells was unclear . <p> A new study by an international team including University of Maryland scientists reveals that a protein called OSCA1.3 forms a channel that leaks calcium into the cells surrounding a plant 's pores , and they determined that a known immune system protein triggers the process . <p> The findings are a major step toward understanding the defense mechanisms plants use to resist infection , which could eventually lead to healthier , more resistant and more productive crops . The research paper was published on August 26 , 2020 in the journal Nature . <p> " This is a major advance , because a substantial part of the world 's food generated by agriculture is lost to pathogens , and we now know the @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ signals for plant immune response to pathogens -- the calcium burst after infection , " said Jos ? Feij ? , a professor of cell biology and molecular genetics at UMD and co-author of the study . " Finding the mechanism associated with this calcium channel allows further research into its regulation , which will improve our understanding of the way in which the channel activity modulates and , eventually , boosts the immune reaction of plants to pathogens . " <p> Plant pores -- called stomata -- are encircled by two guard cells , which respond to calcium signals that tell the cells to expand or contract and trigger innate immune signals , initiating the plant 's defense response . Because calcium can not pass directly through the guard cell membranes , scientists knew a calcium channel had to be at work . But they did n't know which protein acted as the calcium channel . <p> To find this protein , the study 's lead author , Cyril Zipfel , a professor of molecular and cellular plant physiology at the University of Zurich and Senior Group Leader at @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ would be modified by another protein named BIK1 , which genetic studies and bioassays identified as a necessary component of the immune calcium response in plants . <p> When exposed to BIK1 , one protein called OSCA1.3 transformed in a very specific way that suggested it could be a calcium channel for plants . OSCA1.3 is a member of a widespread family of proteins known to exist as ion channels in many organisms , including humans , and it seems to be specifically activated upon detection of pathogens . <p> To determine if OSCA1.3 was , in fact , the calcium channel he was looking for , Zipfel 's team reached out to Feij ? , who is also an affiliate professor in the College of Agriculture and Natural Resources at UMD and is well known for identifying and characterizing novel ion channels and signaling mechanisms in plants . Erwan Michard , a visiting assistant research scientist in Feij ? " This fundamental knowledge is badly needed to inform ecology and agriculture on how the biome will react to the climatic changes that our planet is going through . " <p> Feij ? will now incorporate this new knowledge of the OSCA1.3 calcium channel into other areas of research in his lab , which is working to understand how the mineral calcium was co-opted through evolution by all living organisms to serve as a signaling device for information about stressors from infection to climate change . <p> " Despite the physiological and ecological relevance of stomatal closure , the identity of some of the key components mediating this closure were still unknown , " Zipfel said . Hold that thought . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Now , what would you think if the sole director of that same private Toronto-based charitable foundation now wants greater control over another charity , this one in Ottawa &amp;mdash ; the Ottawa Senators Foundation ? You good with that ? Again , hold that thought . First , some background : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; We are witnessing the start of a blistering fight between the franchise&amp;rsquo ; s enigmatic owner , Eugene Melnyk , who never seems to miss a chance to do the wrong thing on the PR front , and the team&amp;rsquo ; s charitable foundation , which just happens to enjoy broad community support . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The fight is for nothing less than control of the Sens Foundation and the allocation of millions of dollars it dispenses to worthy causes every year . And the fight could get very messy . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Melnyk has long agitated for more say in the foundation&amp;rsquo ; s operations , including deciding where all the money goes after the bills are paid . He wants to broaden the list of prospective recipients beyond local youth-related programs that are currently funded to embrace causes closer to his own heart , like organ donation awareness . That&amp;rsquo ; s not surprising , given that he narrowly survived a liver transplant in 2015 . But the manner in which he is going about it has a growing number of community leaders worried and angry . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The team recently warned the Sens Foundation that it will either start marching to Melnyk&amp;rsquo ; s drum or be replaced by a new charitable organization that will . Last week , the foundation&amp;rsquo ; s voluntary board of directors , which prides itself in its independence providing community oversight , responded with a polite &amp;ldquo ; No thanks . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Unless the differences are resolved , the two sides will officially part ways July 31 , leaving Melnyk in search of a new charitable foundation more to his liking while the existing one embarks on a very uncertain future independent of the hockey team . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The team&amp;rsquo ; s new president of business operations , Anthony Leblanc , told Postmedia&amp;rsquo ; s Bruce Garrioch on Friday the team just wants to make the Sens foundation more efficient so more money can be invested in good causes , like organ donation awareness . Leblanc has been on the job seven weeks and you&amp;rsquo ; d think he&amp;rsquo ; d have bigger fish to fry , given the team&amp;rsquo ; s myriad challenges on and off ice . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Undaunted , Leblanc cited a since-widely disputed 2018 Charity Intelligence Report which gave the Sens foundation a C- grade for spending about half what it raises on programs . The findings were controversial , in part because of the manner in which it calculates expenses related to 50/50 draws . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Charity Intelligence does not always hit the mark in assessing charities . Last year , it apologized to the Winnipeg Jets foundation for , among other reasons , misrepresenting its revenue reporting . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Still , Leblanc insisted the Sens Foundation should be spending closer to 70-80 cents of each dollar raised , a near-impossible benchmark when half the proceeds of a simple 50/50 draw are deemed to be an expense . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Also , it&amp;rsquo ; s tough for the foundation to keep up with some other like-minded sports-related charities when some Canadian NHL teams cover the rent and even the salaries of their foundations&amp;rsquo ; employees . The Sens Foundation , meanwhile , is assessed hundreds of thousands of dollars in HR , IT , finance and rent costs annually , according to individuals familiar with the situation . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The real issue isn&amp;rsquo ; t costs . It&amp;rsquo ; s about control of the foundation&amp;rsquo ; s operations , including where it dispenses the cash . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The foundation didn&amp;rsquo ; t entirely ignored Melnyk&amp;rsquo ; s appeal to flow at least some cash into organ donation awareness . In 2018 , against its better judgment , perhaps , it budgeted $100,000 , plus an additional $15,000 in sponsorships , to The Organ Project ( TOP ) , a Toronto-based private charitable foundation set up by Melnyk in 2016 to manage his pet project &amp;mdash ; creating greater awareness about organ donations and waiting lists . Ultimately , the $100,00 was never sent . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; According to Canada Revenue Agency filings , the Organ Donation Project generated&amp;nbsp ; $991,708 in revenues in 2018 , primarily thanks to a big charity gala it staged in Toronto . No doubt , that $100,000 Senators Foundation cheque helped . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So what happened to all that money ? Again , according to CRA filings , The Organ Project invested barely $5,000 of the nearly $1 million it raised on organ donor awareness . For those without a calculator , that&amp;rsquo ; s 0.49 per cent , or less than half a cent for every dollar raised . And yet the Sens Foundation is being attacked for investing about 50 cents on every dollar it raises on programs . The hypocrisy is stunning . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So , where did all The Organ Project money go if not to worthy causes ? According to CRA , &amp;nbsp ; a whopping $779,464 went to cover fundraising costs . Another $238,118 went to management and administration . I&amp;rsquo ; m told these are the kind of results almost certain to draw the attention of the taxman. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Organ Project is registered as a &amp;ldquo ; private foundation&amp;rdquo ; and , as such does not require an arm&amp;rsquo ; s length community board of directors overseeing operations as does the Ottawa Senators Foundation . Instead , it appears to have only one director : Eugene Melnyk. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Organ Project shut down last year with a promise to re-launch this spring . That hasn&amp;rsquo ; t happened . Its Toronto office is closed and there doesn&amp;rsquo ; t appear to be anybody left on the payroll . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Its balance sheet lists $201,378 in assets and $391,655 in liabilities , including&amp;nbsp ; a $224,902 unpaid debt to someone with a &amp;ldquo ; non-arm&amp;rsquo ; s length&amp;rdquo ; relationship with the private foundation , according to the CRA filing . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So , who do you want overseeing the important work of the Senators Foundation ? Golfers anxious for go-ahead to get back into the swing of thingshttp : **34;25128;TOOLONG ... src= " https : **34;25164;TOOLONG ... title= " ( Getty Images ) " alt= " ( Getty Images ) " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;25200;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 574417 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Golfers in Ottawa , me included , are counting on Premier Doug Ford to answer our collective prayers this week by releasing us from household captivity to resume a favourite pastime , albeit under different rules and absent some of the sport&amp;rsquo ; s long-held traditions . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Forget the handshakes and post-game clubhouse beers . There&amp;rsquo ; ll be no rakes in the bunkers or even pins on the greens . Even the golf cups will be replaced by a protruding target , all of it aimed at limiting players&amp;rsquo ; contact with potentially germ-carrying surfaces . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Practice ranges will be closed . There&amp;rsquo ; ll be restrictions on the use of motorized golf carts and extra time allotted to each group so as to build distance from other players . All of this , of course , assuming Ford follows the sensible lead of some other provinces that have already given the green light to golfers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At this point , golfers are ready to accept whatever it takes so long as they can get back into the swing of things . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Whichever way Ford goes on the issue , the decision is likely to be controversial . Opening courses means golfers will be free to stroll the lush greenery of a private golf course while urban dwellers continue to be denied access to their own community parks . But keeping courses closed , even for another month or two , will tee-off many golfers who insist the sport is a healthy and safe way to get through the current quarantine , both mentally and physically . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A negative decision will also spell financial disaster for an industry that already operates with thin profit margins and has only a few precious months to make its annual revenues . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Right now , courses in Ottawa are reporting superb conditions after a relatively light winter . Some would have enjoyed the earliest openings in years had COVID-19 not thrown a duck-hook in their game plans . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; If golf courses aren&amp;rsquo ; t allowed to open until June , you will likely see some not survive , &amp;rdquo ; says Andy Rajhathy , a local PGA professional and vice president of ClubEG , a company that organizes golf leagues and tournaments and offers discounted green fees to dozens of local courses for its members . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; This spring would have been a great opportunity for courses to catch up , &amp;rdquo ; after a few bad years that have strained profit margins , Rajhathy said in an interview . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The golf industry has not been easy the past decade . Margins are small ( and ) expenses are higher than ever . While we still see a great amount of golfers , the weather is such a major factor that in recent years it&amp;rsquo ; s been tough to get ahead . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The PGA of Canada and National Golf Course Owners have worked with provincial governments to set new standards of play to minimize risks of spreading the virus while giving golfers a much-needed break from social isolation in a healthy outdoor environment . The industry has requested an opening date of May 12 , although some industry insiders expect the official opening will be held till May 19 provided courses abide by the precautions . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Across the region , golf courses have been cutting greens and fertilizing fairways in hopes of an eventual opening , but even absent such approval , the courses have no choice but to incur big expenses maintaining their courses lest they surrender to weeds and overgrowth. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That means many costs are being incurred without the guarantee of revenue to cover the expenses . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Courses depend heavily on membership fees as a primary revenue source . Amazingly , I didn&amp;rsquo ; t even know that some of my friends knew her . She was a stealthy fairy . And I am grateful to have been on the receiving end of her magic . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One of her favourite jobs was for the Children&amp;rsquo ; s Wish Foundation of Canada Ottawa Chapter where she helped make dreams come true for dozens of children with life-limiting illnesses . Yet he made no specific mention of cancelled trains or frozen switches in his annual address to council . Not even a passing reference to any one of a thousand other problems that have plagued the daily commute for thousands of Ottawans , prompting calls in some quarters for the heads of anyone involved in approving the system . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Watson&amp;rsquo ; s State of the City approach to the transit crisis reminded me of the immortal words of philosopher king Alfred E. Don&amp;rsquo ; t fan the flames . Sisterly love , stem cells and overwhelming happinesshttp : **31;31366;TOOLONG ... src= " https : **34;31399;TOOLONG ... title= " Vicki Baer and her sister Michelle Hollett. " alt= " Vicki Baer and her sister Michelle Hollett. " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;31435;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 554648 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; On Christmas Day two sisters received what has to be one of the best gifts ever &amp;mdash ; news that one could potentially save the life of the other . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Michelle Hollett of Ottawa is a stem cell transplant match for her sister , Vicki Baer . While she isn&amp;rsquo ; t a perfect match , a donation from a sibling would stand a better chance of being accepted by the recipient&amp;rsquo ; s body . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I was surprised and elated . Hearing that Michelle was a match brought instant tears of joy . I was ready to start the next phase of treatment . I felt so grateful that she was able to save me , &amp;rdquo ; Baer said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She was diagnosed in October with acute myeloid leukemia after waking up with a black eye after suffering months of exhaustion . She called her sister who remembered the story of Ottawa radio personality Stuntman Stu who credits a pharmacist for saving his life by suggesting he go directly to the hospital for having similar strange symptoms . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As Baer had dealt with Crohn&amp;rsquo ; s disease for 14 years it was originally thought her symptoms could be related to that . But Hollett had a feeling it wasn&amp;rsquo ; t and a bone marrow biopsy and a round of tests confirmed it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; As she was checking in with hospital reception , I started to cry , looked at her best friend and said I&amp;rsquo ; m afraid they won&amp;rsquo ; t let her leave today . This whole time I&amp;rsquo ; m thinking that Kitchener is a great place for Oktoberfest , but I was going to convince her to come to Ottawa to have her treatment . After all , it worked for Stuntman Stu , &amp;rdquo ; Hollett said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; However , the sisters learned there was no time . Hollett said they were told by the doctor , &amp;ldquo ; There is a chance you do not make it . You are very sick , but I have a plan . You can go home to get some clothes , say bye to your dog , but you will be admitted tonight and we will start chemo right away . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Aggressive chemotherapy was used three times to keep her leukemia controlled until she could have a much needed stem cell transplant.The world-wide hunt for a match began so she could receive the life-saving procedure . It turns out the match was right beside her . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; On Christmas Day , they met with the doctor and Hollett posted the video of that moment on her Facebook ( which is how I learned of this remarkable news ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Before my mum passed away from breast cancer , she asked me to always take care of my sister , &amp;rdquo ; Hollett said . &amp;ldquo ; Being told I was a match to donate my stem cells , and save her life , has been the ultimate gift . It was the Christmas miracle we all dreamt about . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; On Jan. 24 , she begins the harvesting process and if they can&amp;rsquo ; t get enough stem cells through her blood , by boosting production with drugs , they will move to a full bone marrow transplant . Baer will require 6 weeks of post-procedure time in hospital . She will have no immune system for a while and will be very vulnerable . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; During this process only one perfect match was found in the entire world , someone who had volunteered for the unrelated bone marrow donor registry , a critically important program . In this country it&amp;rsquo ; s run by Canadian Blood Services . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And that&amp;rsquo ; s how Stuntman Stu was matched with a stranger who saved his life . He had hoped telling his story would help others . He told me upon hearing this story of sisterly love , &amp;ldquo ; Sharing my cancer journey helped me face my fear , which translated into many hearing my story of what to do , if in fact they were in a similar situation . A lesson learned is a lesson shared . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The sisters hope their story will encourage more people to register , and there is a need for more men and people from ethnically diverse groups . I was on the list until I aged out of the program and it&amp;rsquo ; s a simple blood test . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When asked how she felt Hollett said : &amp;ldquo ; Overwhelming happiness and relief that soon this nightmare will be over and life will eventually get back to normal . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; Kimothy WalkerFri , 17 Jan 2020 19:59:01 **45;31465;TOOLONG ... " alt= " A company in Brantford is one of many seeking to hire new employees . " data-portal-copyright= " Brian Thompson " **28;31582;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 554808 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Last year was a tremendously successful one in Ontario for job creation , and the numbers prove it . Statistics Canada could not have stated it any better , announcing &amp;ldquo ; Full-time employment growth in Canada driven by gains in Ontario . &amp;rdquo ; Nationally , there were 320,000 net new jobs added last year ( mostly full-time ) , with 243,000 created in Ontario . That&amp;rsquo ; s 76 per cent of all jobs created in Canada , despite being home to 38 per cent of the population . Not only that , but the 3.3 per cent year-over-year growth was the strongest seen in a December in Ontario in 32 years . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In December , Canada&amp;rsquo ; s employment increased by 35,000 and again , it was led by gains in Ontario of more than 25,000 net new jobs . The bulk of that growth was full-time , private-sector jobs , sending the jobless rate to 5.3 per cent . There is no question that Ontario is leading the nation in job creation , but make no mistake &amp;mdash ; this did not happen by accident . These numbers are a direct result of the Ford government lowering the cost of doing business in Ontario . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Our government is implementing a plan to attract investment , encourage innovation , grow small businesses , and create quality jobs across the province . Ontario is supporting small- and medium-sized businesses by creating a business-friendly environment through lowering taxes and other costs , and reducing the burden of red tape . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Actions such as lowering the small business tax rate by 8.7 per cent have saved 275,000 owners up to $1,500 annually . Reducing WSIB premium rates by 30 per cent in 2019 and a further 17 per cent in 2020 saves Ontario businesses over $2 billion annually . Allowing for in-year write-offs of capital investments saves our manufacturers a further $700 million annually . These and other tax and cost reductions have saved Ontario businesses $5 billion in 2019 and will save them $5.4 billion in 2020 . And the business community reacted exactly as predicted &amp;mdash ; they used those funds to hire nearly 300,000 new employees since our government took office in 2018. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But we know there is always more to do , given we live in a globally-competitive world . Through the recent Better for People , Smarter for Business Act , we continue to lower the regulatory burden of red tape . We will bring further red tape reduction bills to the Legislature two times every year , because we want Ontario to be even more cost effective and efficient so that our job creators can succeed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As part of our plan to create a more competitive business environment , we announced the formation of the Premier&amp;rsquo ; s Advisory Council on Competitiveness . The Council will consult with business leaders , speak directly with private-sector workers , and leverage lessons from peer jurisdictions to understand how to improve Ontario&amp;rsquo ; s competitiveness . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There are other initiatives underway , such as Driving Prosperity ; the plan to set out a 10-year vision for how industry , the research and education sector , and all three levels of government can work together to strengthen the auto sector&amp;rsquo ; s competitiveness . That strategy already identified a Job Site Challenge , launched this year , as an opportunity to help create a competitive business environment and put the province back on the short-list of candidates for major upcoming automotive and advanced manufacturing investments . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; All these actions send a message to job creators in Ontario and across the world that Ontario is open for business and open for jobs . Every action taken by our government to improve the business climate in Ontario has resulted in job numbers climbing , unemployment plummeting , and more people who weren&amp;rsquo ; t working , getting back in our communities contributing to our province . Ontario&amp;rsquo ; s economic development is looking better than ever in 2020 thanks to the many hardworking Ontarians who have now rejoined the workforce to build Ontario together . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Vic Fedeli is Ontario 's minister of economic development , job creation and trade . &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;31612;TOOLONG ... Friday was one of them . I&amp;rsquo ; d just penned a brilliant article on how hiring a new CEO was more important to the future of the Ottawa Senators than signing any of their looming free agents when , lo and behold , the team announced exactly that . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As the new CEO , former Shaw Communications executive Jim Little becomes the business face of the franchise , filling a critical role left vacant two years ago , when veteran hockey executive Tom Anselmi bolted for the exits only a year into the job . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Let&amp;rsquo ; s hope Little has a little more stamina . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; His bio suggests he left Shaw nearly two years ago and gives no indication what he has done since . I just hope he has good spidey senses when it comes to reading the local fan base . I also hope franchise owner Eugene Melnyk gives him some breathing room without too many late-night interventions from Barbados . It&amp;rsquo ; s the price of being an absentee owner with absolutely no feel for the local marketplace . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;31868;TOOLONG ... title= " Jim Little was named new CEO of the Ottawa Senators on Friday . For two years , there has been no face to put to the business end of the franchise other than a GM , whose head is rightly buried in postgame videos and who has neither the time nor the skills to worry about falling attendance or good marketing . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In those two years , there has been no one to speak to the broader community about this team other than you-know-who . Yes , Melnyk would make occasional forays into the marketplace , but he would usually end up saying something stupid or controversial , pushing the team&amp;rsquo ; s fan base into another round of hysterics and attendance into the dumpster. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; My point is there has been no one to bang on doors and attend all those early-morning or late-night community events , grabbing every available spotlight to sell the merits of supporting the city&amp;rsquo ; s team . That&amp;rsquo ; s what former team presidents Roy Mlakar and Cyril Leeder were really good at . They knew everybody and everybody knew them and trusted them . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Frankly , I&amp;rsquo ; d have hired Bruce Firestone , the founding owner of the franchise , to be the face of this business in the absence of its real owner , and I&amp;rsquo ; d have armed him with a clear mandate to rebuild the connection with fans . Like most fans , I&amp;rsquo ; d welcome new ownership . But , by now , it has become evident that Melnyk isn&amp;rsquo ; t selling the team anytime soon . Forget all those recurring rumours about an imminent sale . It&amp;rsquo ; s not happening . It&amp;rsquo ; s possible the de facto fan boycott has only strengthened his resolve to keep the franchise . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There&amp;rsquo ; s no quick miracle to turning the franchise around , although hiring a new CEO is a start . Despite trading virtually all my favourite players last year , I&amp;rsquo ; m back as a fan . And I&amp;rsquo ; ve discovered there are plenty of cheap seats . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The new team being assembled is fun to watch and has a few exciting future stars . And some of those boneheaded trades last year are starting to look pretty damn smart . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Few of the former stars the team surrendered to get draft picks aren&amp;rsquo ; t performing all that well with their new teams . Even fan favourite and former captain Erik Karlsson is overpaid and under-performing. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Meantime , the Senators are loaded with draft picks and the future is bright . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;32000;TOOLONG ... title= " Senators owner Eugene Melnyk , middle , skates with children at his 16th annual Eugene Melnyk Skate for Kids at Canadian Tire Centre on Dec. 20. Nor should it . The Senators are my team , damn it . Eugene Melnyk just happens to own it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I still miss Mark Stone . But there are new stars emerging fast and a bright future thanks to a boatload of good draft picks . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Fans have made their point by driving attendance into the dumpster , but it&amp;rsquo ; s a new year and it&amp;rsquo ; s time for a new attitude by the team&amp;rsquo ; s fan base . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Leafs fans survived Harold Ballard just as Yankee fans survived George Steinbrenner and New England Patriot fans will inevitably survive Robert Kraft . More like gobsmacked , actually , if you read the British tabloids in the wake of Prince Harry and wife Meghan Markle&amp;rsquo ; s shocking decision to vacate the Royal household and set up shop on their own , possibly right here in Canada . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Harry , the Duke of Sussex , is even talking about getting a job , for goodness sakes , liberating his family from its current financial dependence on the Royal cheque book . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Here&amp;rsquo ; s a princely idea &amp;mdash ; let&amp;rsquo ; s make him our next governor general . Seriously . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He is perfectly qualified to assume the role of Her Majesty&amp;rsquo ; s official representative in Canada and both he and wife Meghan Markle would bring a certain regal flair and panache to the job . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Besides , we&amp;rsquo ; d be doing Her Majesty a giant favour , given the Royal drama that has enveloped the life of her favourite grandson . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s not like being governor general of Canada would be a steep learning curve for someone who has grown up in a world gilded by history , ceremony and constitutional protocol . He&amp;rsquo ; s perfect . And while he may not hold Canadian citizenship &amp;mdash ; yet &amp;mdash ; we can work on that . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Lest we forget , Canada only started hiring Canadian-born citizens for the job in 1952 . In other words , for the first 85 years of our independence , governors general were plucked from a smoky backroom of British ambassadors or members of the House of Lords . ( You may recall a certain Lord Stanley even dedicated a cup to recognize hockey supremacy. ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As a senior member of the royal family , Harry would be a huge step up from that period in our history . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Think about it : He would make a wonderful honorary commander-in-chief for our armed forces , having served during two deployments in Afghanistan . He has since launched the annual Invictus Games for wounded warriors , staged in Toronto in 2017 . Our troops would love him during ceremonial events . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Royal couple seems to have developed a strong fondness for Canada , even before their marriage two years ago . They met in Toronto and have good friendships with people like TV personality Ben Mulroney and his wife , fashion designer and stylist Jessica Brownstein ( their kids participated in the royal wedding ) . Meghan is American , but she has spent many years in Toronto as an actor . They know the place pretty well . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; They&amp;rsquo ; ve spent the past few weeks in Canada contemplating a future away from the searing light of unwanted attention they attract in Britain . For the most part , we have left them alone . Don&amp;rsquo ; t under-estimate how much that is influencing their decision to surrender formal responsibilities in the royal household for a new life elsewhere . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Canada is perfect for them &amp;mdash ; a young interracial immigrant couple looking for a new life . It&amp;rsquo ; s poster worthy . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Now , I&amp;rsquo ; m not trying to force an early exit of the current occupant of Rideau Hall , Julie Payette , although she has been seen as a disappointment in some circles . She still has a couple of years left in her five-year term in office , time that could be well used by Harry to brush up on his Canadian knowledge , learn French and apply for permanent residency , a first step toward eventual citizenship . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; We could probably speed things up a bit if there was any enthusiasm for the idea . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Who knows ? The royal couple may jump at the opportunity to stay in the royal lane while liberating themselves from the endless abuse they endure in Britain , especially from all-too-familiar sources &amp;mdash ; the notorious British tabloid media . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; How bad is it ? In a week where much of the world was gripped by the possibility of war between the U.S. and Iran , the British tabloids obsessed over Harry&amp;rsquo ; s decision to give up his royal role . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Headlines decry the &amp;ldquo ; rogue royals&amp;rsquo ; &amp;rsquo ; and accuse Harry and Meghan of being &amp;ldquo ; spoiled brats . &amp;rdquo ; The &lt;em&gt;Daily Mail&lt;/em&gt; devoted more than a dozen pages of breathless analysis about Harry and Meghan&amp;rsquo ; s break with the family business and how it has created a veritable royal rumble at Buckingham Palace . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Attention has reached Diana-like proportions as royalists fever over what all this could mean for the royal household . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For Harry , it must bring back horrible memories of his mother&amp;rsquo ; s death amid a familiar media frenzy over her life choices . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For the Queen , the situation must rekindle her own painful memories of the abdication of her uncle , Edward VIII , who chose the love of an American divorcee over remaining as king . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Brits learned nothing from the tragedy of Princess Diana . Alas , the hounding will only get worse now that Harry has announced he wants out . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Come to Canada , Harry . Lustre 's off Canada , but maybe it should still be therehttp : **35;32456;TOOLONG ... src= " https : **34;32493;TOOLONG ... title= " Ottawa . " alt= " Ottawa . " data-portal-copyright= " JULIE OLIVER " **28;32529;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 519373 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Happy New Year , Happy New Decade . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So the country is feeling a little worse for wear these days , but at least we survived the last decade without wrecking the place . The question is this : What will it take to shake off a hangover and restore our once lofty reputation as Best Country in the World , assuming we ever deserved that title . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; You&amp;rsquo ; ll recall that , for the better part of the 1990s , Canada stood proudly atop the United Nations&amp;rsquo ; annual Human Development Index . We bragged to anyone who&amp;rsquo ; d listen that Canada was the Best Country in the World . We were No. 1 ! &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It was a national shock when we slipped to second place one year . Wind forward to 2010 and the Good Ship Canada began to take on water . We dropped to fourth . By last year , we&amp;rsquo ; d plunged to 13th. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So what happened ? Why was nobody cheering for Canada anymore ? Are we doing something wrong because , by almost any account , we are still doing very well compared to the rest of the world ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; We are still the most educated country on the planet . We&amp;rsquo ; re among the more wealthy . Unemployment is at historic lows and average incomes compare favourably to much of the world . We lead long lives and , according to one study , are among the happiest citizens on Earth , although you wouldn&amp;rsquo ; t know that if you followed our politics or almost any news headlines of late . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Crime in Canada is up . That&amp;rsquo ; s not good . But overall crime rates are still well below rates of a decade earlier . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Maybe the most under-reported story of the decade concerns the drop in poverty rates in Canada . Poverty is now at its lowest in history in our country , below 10 per cent . That is a remarkable achievement and needs to be celebrated even while our international reputation is taking a bit of a hit of late . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Maybe it was just a change in how certain criteria was applied by the UN or maybe the UN just wanted to spread the love a little more widely since Canada dominated the rankings for so many years and Canadians abused that recognition by bragging to the world at every opportunity . Whatever the reason , we can no longer point to the UN&amp;rsquo ; s annual ranking to stake our claim as a moral leader to the world . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But not all is lost . An annual Quality of Life ranking produced by U.S. News &amp;amp ; World Report has , for the fourth year running , placed us among the top three countries in which to live , although something called CEO World Magazine clocked us in no better than 18th . It&amp;rsquo ; s all in the eye of the beholder , I guess . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While Canada&amp;rsquo ; s reputation has taken a hit internationally , some of our cities , including our own , are doing just fine . International business consultancy firm Mercer ranked five Canadian cities highly in its annual list of best cities for quality of living and doing business . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ottawa clocked in at 19th , while Vancouver led Canadian cities with an impressive third-place ranking . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; We&amp;rsquo ; ll certainly take the love where we can find it , and you can find it if you search hard enough . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A website catering to international adventurers ranks Canada third in the world for travel adventures , while a magazine catering to gay tourists ranks Canada the most gay friendly country on the planet . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A major international moving company also recently declared Ottawa the best place for immigrants to relocate , while an international auto parts retailer produced its own survey declaring our city among the best for drivers , probably because they aren&amp;rsquo ; t selling enough parts to local auto body repair shops in Ottawa . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; We&amp;rsquo ; ll take the compliments wherever we can . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ottawa continues to enjoy a strong reputation within Canada as a good place to live and work , and we need to work hard to retain that title . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Over the decade , Ottawa slipped from first to second in the annual Moneysense Magazine rating of the most livable cities in Canada , but still rates at the top on a range of categories , including strength of the local economy , relatively low crime rates and housing affordability. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Last year , the city&amp;rsquo ; s population surpassed the one-million mark , placing us in a different league of big cities with unique problems and a new set of challenges . It won&amp;rsquo ; t be easy to maintain Ottawa&amp;rsquo ; s reputation as a great place to live , work and raise families . Or Canada&amp;rsquo ; s for that matter . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Now , there&amp;rsquo ; s a challenge for the decade ahead : Let&amp;rsquo ; s Make Canada Great Again . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Rick Gibbons is a veteran journalist/broadcaster and former publisher and chief executive of the Ottawa Sun&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **31;32559;TOOLONG " **38;32592;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;32632;TOOLONG ... family matriarch Diane Ford passes away&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;32667;TOOLONG ... How are beauty pageants still a thing in 2020 ? http : **35;32784;TOOLONG ... src= " https : **34;32821;TOOLONG ... title= " Miss World takes place in London with 104 countries represented . " alt= " Miss World takes place in London with 104 countries represented . " data-portal-copyright= " TSAA/ZDS ... **28;32857;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 551266 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Imagine if a man was disqualified from a beauty pageant because organizers didn&amp;rsquo ; t think he could perform his duties in a professional manner because he was a father , and had been married . Seems unlikely , right ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That&amp;rsquo ; s what happened to Miss Ukraine , Veronika Didusenko , who is now taking on the Miss World competition in court for violating her rights . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She said on Instagram : &amp;ldquo ; The Equality Act protects against discrimination based on certain characteristics , including marriage , maternity and sex . Denying me the chance of competing on those bases breaches those protections against discrimination . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I find it odd to even conceive of young childless never-married men parading on a stage and demonstrating their ability to answer questions about current affairs while being physically beautiful . The idea that parenthood or marriage makes one less capable of these tasks is , frankly , ridiculous . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The story broke around the time that a video went viral depicting Miss Nigeria&amp;rsquo ; s excitement over her competitor&amp;rsquo ; s winning Miss Universe . It was actually international news that a woman would show profound enthusiasm for another woman ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s 2020 now . An industry dedicated to judging women on their physical characteristics seems outdated . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So why do pageants exist ? They have an audience , that&amp;rsquo ; s why . Television ratings fuel advertising revenue . If nobody watches , there are no advertisers and shows are cancelled . It&amp;rsquo ; s that simple . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Now , I realize I contribute to a newspaper chain that still has a &amp;ldquo ; Sunshine Girl&amp;rdquo ; though not in this paper&amp;rsquo ; s print version ; it is available on the website . What a woman in a sexy Santa costume has to do with journalism is beyond me , but people click , and that matters for sales . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I rarely invite social media input because it&amp;rsquo ; s nasty , but can a single person give me a reason why we parade women around on a stage ? A scholarship ? That&amp;rsquo ; s what I call &amp;ldquo ; spin&amp;rdquo ; . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In all the boardrooms I visit , body tape to keep a bathing suit in place has never been a discussed strategy . Decisions about cosmetic surgery are private and not check marks in a box . I get Botox and I&amp;rsquo ; m very open about it , but several women have gone public about being strongly encouraged by pageant organizers to do major surgery . Success should never be correlated to cosmetic surgery . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In full transparency , I was Miss Teen Ottawa , only because the 16-year-old winner had to move away . So , as the 15-year-old first runner up I was promoted . That was 1983 . This is now 2020 . Times have changed . Back then nobody thought twice about teenaged girls on stage in spandex aerobic outfits at a local mall and social media didn&amp;rsquo ; t exist . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Would I encourage my daughter to enter a beauty pageant ? CTV Ottawa 's latest departures mark the end of an erahttp : **37;33109;TOOLONG ... src= " https : **34;33148;TOOLONG ... title= " After 33 years with CTV Ottawa , Terry Marcotte has had a front row seat for some of the city 's biggest sporting events for almost four decades , but it 's the unknowns in sports he loved to cover , he says . " alt= " After 33 years with CTV Ottawa , Terry Marcotte has had a front row seat for some of the city 's biggest sporting events for almost four decades , but it 's the unknowns in sports he loved to cover , he says . " data-portal-copyright= " Julie Oliver " **28;33184;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 548253 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Familiar faces are fast disappearing from our local TV airwaves . The latest departures provide a final exclamation point to a brutal decade of media cutbacks that have ripped like a hacksaw across all traditional media platforms and left the communities they serve the poorer for it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; These latest departures &amp;mdash ; all from CTV Ottawa ( formerly CJOH ) &amp;mdash ; seem especially poignant as they impact veteran TV personalities who became household names over a generation as we welcomed them into our living rooms during local TV newscasts . They also willingly embraced leading roles beyond the TV lights in support of countless charitable and other community endeavours . For all of that , they will be missed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It seems only fitting then that Terry Marcotte , Catherine Lathem , Joanne Schnurr and Michael O&amp;rsquo ; Byrne should wind down their careers together in the dying days of this decade , if only because they went through so much together during careers spanning nearly 40 years . They developed their skills together and enjoyed countless successes under the leadership of their mentor , the late Max Keeping , who had a knack for moulding unvarnished talent . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; They endured their share of terrible tragedies too , none worse than the senseless , cold-blooded shooting death of their colleague , Brian Smith , who was gunned down in 1995 by a psychotic in the parking lot of the old CJOH building on Merivale Road . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I remember vividly how that CJOH news team pulled together to cover the story and how their grief became the grief of an entire community . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The era of CJOH dominance seemed to crest about the time its Merivale offices and studios burned down in 2010 , forcing the entire crew into an uncomfortable early marriage with their crosstown CTV affiliate , The NewRO . The fire destroyed decades of film and audio material . The station never seemed the same after that . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But in their heyday , the CJOH team dominated the local airways , crushing the local CBC station , sometimes 10:1 in ratings . &amp;nbsp ; While most big city local TV newsrooms depended on pretty faces and hairspray for their ratings , Max Keeping&amp;rsquo ; s team banked on a much different formula . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Keeping&amp;rsquo ; s secret was finding people with whom the community could identify ; often local people who could create compelling narratives , not just 40-second news clips , and who understood that with elevated public profiles came certain responsibilities to give back to the community . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Often his young charges lacked the polish , the big hair and giant egos of big city stations . But it didn&amp;rsquo ; t seem to matter . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Marcotte admitted in interviews this week he was not exactly the perfect TV stereotype and wasn&amp;rsquo ; t even a great broadcaster . Yet that was exactly what endeared him to TV viewers &amp;mdash ; an honest , authentic storyteller who found value in telling the stories of local athletes who developed their skills at community rinks or in local parks and who often beat all odds to enjoy their share of success . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In addition to his news anchor job , O&amp;rsquo ; Byrne has also played a huge role in helping charities raise money and expand their reach . He has received numerous honours in the process , including a Governor General&amp;rsquo ; s Award , for his community work . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Some organizers in the charitable sector worry about losing this type of community asset who could bring their energy and high profile to help organizations in need . The team also happened to produce good journalists , too . Catherine Lathem and Joanne Schnurr will be sorely missed in that regard . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The media landscape has changed dramatically over the decade , thanks to a digital age and the new competition for advertising dollars that came with it . Local TV newscasts neatly packaged to serve a dinnertime audience no longer carry the same punch in a world with never-ending news cycles and an insatiable demand for immediate news . But in their day , they reached large audiences and , in the case of CJOH , could bring the entire community together . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; These latest CTV Ottawa departures follow a decision announced last spring to change the traditional job of reporting staff . In future , reporters will become video journalists who will not only report , but operate cameras , too , and even edit their work . For many older veterans of the newsroom , the decision was either adapt to the times or move on . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; We wish them well . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Gibbons is a veteran journalist/broadcaster and former publisher and chief executive of the Ottawa Sun . &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **31;33214;TOOLONG " **38;33247;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;33287;TOOLONG ... Family , friends , rivals and community say goodbye to Tommy Cavanaghhttp : **32;33439;TOOLONG ... src= " https : **34;33473;TOOLONG ... title= " Funeral party for Thomas Cavanagh.
