" data-portal-copyright= " Jean Levac " **28;33509;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 547213 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; He was widely known simply as &amp;ldquo ; Tommy . &amp;rdquo ; And don&amp;rsquo ; t let the work boots and gruff demeanour fool you . Or the formal education that stopped somewhere around Grade 6 after he bolted from his one-room school house rather than face the strap for something he didn&amp;rsquo ; t do &amp;mdash ; smoking . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Thomas Cavanagh was a character all right , but he was also among the most colourful and successful entrepreneurs this region has ever seen . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Cavanagh died last week at the age of 86 . On Thursday , his remarkable life was celebrated in grand style with family and friends , community leaders , even business rivals , who gathering for tributes and to share stories . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Even Mayor Jim Watson slipped outside the city&amp;rsquo ; s boundaries into Beckwith Township near Carleton Place to join more than a thousand mourners for an emotional service at an indoor community sports field . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It was a perfect setting . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Giant Cavanagh construction trucks framed the dais , creating just the right staging for a service commemorating the life of a man whose name and accomplishments will be forever tied to the local construction business . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There were stirring tributes to the entrepreneurial spirit of a man who started from humble roots with only a single axle dump truck and , over the next 66 years , built a family-owned and -operated construction giant , employing more than 800 workers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The event was billed as Cavanagh&amp;rsquo ; s very own &amp;ldquo ; Farewell Party&amp;rdquo ; and , true to his Irish roots , there was music and as many laughs as tears among the attendees. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Son Jeff Cavanagh described how his father&amp;rsquo ; s first job was delivering coal and when he encountered a poor resident who couldn&amp;rsquo ; t afford to heat his home , he would give the coal away for free . Needless to say , Jeff noted , Tommy didn&amp;rsquo ; t last long in that endeavour . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Thanks goodness for that . He turned his attention to building his own business . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Though he shied from public recognition , Cavanagh&amp;rsquo ; s generosity was well known , especially in the rural communities where he&amp;rsquo ; d build a sports field or buy tables for charitable causes . He contributed to many local events like the Carp Fair and make sure people in need were given a helping hand &amp;mdash ; often with a job . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; He taught us how to work hard and how to play hard , &amp;rdquo ; Cavanagh said . &amp;nbsp ; &amp;ldquo ; I always wanted to make my dad proud . He was my dad , my friend and my business partner . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He said that in recent years he has stood back and marvelled what the family has built under his father&amp;rsquo ; s leadership . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The company&amp;rsquo ; s teal-coloured trucks are a common sight on highways and back roads throughout the region , especially in the city&amp;rsquo ; s far west-end where the company has its headquarters along Highway 7 , near Carleton Place . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But travel almost anywhere in these parts and you&amp;rsquo ; re almost certainly driving on roads built by Cavanagh Construction . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The company owns 40 pits from which it harvests vast quantities of sand and gravel used to build everything from highways to suburban driveways . Over the years , the company has diversified to building housing developments , even into green energy projects , including a small hydro facility the company revitalized in Almonte. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One industry observer described honesty and loyalty as the keys to Cavanagh&amp;rsquo ; s business success . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Despite that success , Cavanagh never lost touch with the business end of a shovel . He remained true to his hard-hat roots , despite enjoying the kind of financial success that could otherwise have funded a lavish lifestyle . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; He chose to live like the people he employed , &amp;rdquo ; one attendee mused . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s no secret that sometimes you agree with him , sometimes you don&amp;rsquo ; t , &amp;rdquo ; said Ottawa Coun. Eli El-Chantiry , who had numerous interactions with Cavanagh. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; But , nevertheless , he always had the community in his heart . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Cavanagh&amp;rsquo ; s tendency to drive fast became legendary among those who knew him . El-Chantiry recalled an incident where he relayed a community complaint to Cavanagh&amp;rsquo ; s office that company vehicles were driving too fast along a country road . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Jeff Cavanagh agreed to set up a speed trap to measure the number of speeders and later reported they had captured only one &amp;mdash ; his dad . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Cavanagh&amp;rsquo ; s casket departed Thursday&amp;rsquo ; s ceremony aboard a large company flat-bed truck normally used to transport heavy equipment . This time it was a personal journey to his final resting place in Beckwith Township . But not before one last drive through the company&amp;rsquo ; s work yards where dozens of trucks and many employees stood in tribute to the boss . You can bet Tommy would have heartily approved . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Meantime , in another part of town , a dozen kilometres away , a rival construction firm ran a Cavanagh company flag up the flagpole , a fitting tribute to a respected adversary . It also criticizes him for being MIA in his College Ward since allegations surfaced in August , including claims that he asked an employee to go braless and assigned other female staffers to dress provocatively while being dispatched to strip clubs in search of dirt on council colleagues . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Since August of 2019 , the councillor has not shown up to council and committee meetings , leaving his constituents struggling without proper representation , &amp;rdquo ; the petition reads . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; He has only made a perfunctory appearance in November 2019 , seemingly to avoid being obliged to give up his seat on city council . For these reasons , we believe it imperative that the councillor resign immediately . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And there is still more bad news for the councillor . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A major sponsor of his annual alcohol-free New Year&amp;rsquo ; s Eve bash , which draws up to 10,000 residents , has withdrawn its support for the event , which features free sleigh rides , fireworks and more . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Chiarelli spends extraordinary time and effort organizing the event each year and deploys dozens of student volunteers from the local school where his wife teaches . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The event is slated to go ahead this year , despite Chiarelli&amp;rsquo ; s troubles . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; However , Giant Tiger , the locally owned department store , has decided to withdraw its traditional sponsorship &amp;ldquo ; due in large part to our values , business needs and scheduling , &amp;rdquo ; according to Alison Scarlett , the company&amp;rsquo ; s director of brand communications . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; At Giant Tiger we evaluate sponsorship opportunities that meet our business needs and align with our values , &amp;rdquo ; she said in an email this week . &amp;ldquo ; We have chosen not to sponsor Rick Chiarelli&amp;rsquo ; s 2019 New Year&amp;rsquo ; s Eve event this year . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She declined to say how much money the company contributed to the event annually , although it&amp;rsquo ; s believed the evening costs nearly $20,000 to stage . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So , how is Chiarelli spending his time these days ? Last week , I mentioned a weird video he posted on social media featuring a tap-dancing marionette . This week , there&amp;rsquo ; s a new YouTube video making the rounds at city hall featuring Chiarelli providing voice-over commentary as one of his daughters applies her makeup . The power of a proper apologyhttp : **33;34926;TOOLONG ... src= " https : **34;34961;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;34997;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 543503 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; As Canadians we are often characterized as saying &amp;ldquo ; sorry&amp;rdquo ; with reckless abandon , but the quality of that intention is important . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Over the past few weeks , when news was very much about apologies , or lack thereof , I decided to research what my dad , who was a psychologist , used to tell me : There are three fundamental elements of a strong apology . We&amp;rsquo ; ll get to that later . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Experts say good apologies lead to empathy and we sure do need some of that these days . Humans make mistakes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I&amp;rsquo ; m not going to get into the &amp;ldquo ; who said what&amp;rdquo ; on Canadian television . That&amp;rsquo ; s been well documented . I do , however , see this as an opportunity to explore the importance of apologizing and how to do it to build or repair bridges . Yes , there is a right way and a way that misses the mark and can fuel anger . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; According to Beverly Flaxington , the author of several books about professional and personal development , an &amp;ldquo ; if&amp;rdquo ; or a &amp;ldquo ; but&amp;rdquo ; after your apology hasn&amp;rsquo ; t nailed it . &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; m sorry if you were offended&amp;rdquo ; is a good example . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She wrote about what it feels like to the person on the receiving end of such an apology . &amp;ldquo ; The apology implies that they have a problem &amp;mdash ; they were the one who chose to be offended , they were the one with the weak feelings that got easily hurt , they were the one who misinterpreted your actions and interpreted them as hurtful , &amp;rdquo ; she writes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And here&amp;rsquo ; s why we care about apologies hitting the mark . Research shows all kinds of benefits when an apology is well received , including physical symptoms of well-being . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; This is likely because when someone confesses to and apologizes for hurting us , we are then able to develop a new image of that person , &amp;rdquo ; says renowned psychotherapist Beverly Engle. &amp;ldquo ; Instead of seeing him through anger and bitterness , the person&amp;rsquo ; s humility and apology cause us to see ( them ) as a fallible , vulnerable human being . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And that , according to her research is where the empathy begins . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She also wrote in &lt;em&gt;Psychology Today&lt;/em&gt; that research at the National Institute for Healthcare Research in Maryland proved scientifically that apology leads to empathy that , in turn , mediates forgiveness . The subjects were post-secondary students . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So back to the lessons from my father , and these are generally written about across the field of psychology , where he learned them , taught them to me and I taught them to my daughter . If you want to nail an apology it&amp;rsquo ; s about the ingredients of what they call the 3Rs , regret , responsibility and remedy . To be clear , there are no &amp;ldquo ; ifs&amp;rdquo ; and no excuses . You need to own it completely . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Now the reason this was such a major focus for my Dad was because as a child I was terrible at apologizing . I saw it as weakness . I&amp;rsquo ; d even cross my arms to physically brace myself for the words I was going to have to say through gritted teeth while looking at my feet . To this day my ego still screams out when I have to admit I was wrong . But , it&amp;rsquo ; s necessary . It shows strength . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One thing I didn&amp;rsquo ; t agree with in many of the psychology articles is that apologies are considered private because there can be no relationship with an injured party if you don&amp;rsquo ; t know them . I believe that doesn&amp;rsquo ; t capture how we often relate to our Canadian television personalities , and these past few weeks have been a good example of that intense relationship . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I couldn&amp;rsquo ; t find the author of this quote that I came across in my research : &amp;ldquo ; You can apologize over and over , but if your actions don&amp;rsquo ; t change the words become meaningless . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;35027;TOOLONG ... take responsibility ' : Bill Peters apologizes for racial slur&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;35062;TOOLONG ... long-term care homes misusing trespass law to limit family visits ? &lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;35097;TOOLONG ... " data-portal-copyright= " Errol McGihon " **28;35246;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 530517 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Residents of Kanata Lakes got a chance to face their adversary and air their beefs about a controversial development of their local golf course this week and came away no more confident their concerns are being heard . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s a David vs . Goliath battle and they know it . As such , they&amp;rsquo ; d best hunker down for a long and expensive fight . Developers play a long game , much longer than many residents may be prepared for , and time is likely on the developers&amp;rsquo ; side . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At issue is the proposed transformation of the Kanata Lakes Golf Course into a 1,500-unit housing and apartment project . The magnitude of public concerns and the resources developers can bring to the battle were fully on display as about 500 residents packed three briefing sessions staged by the developers . Many residents pushed back hard as a small army of engineers , planners and other experts made some effort to alleviate public concerns . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Alas , many answers provoked collective gasps , occasional snorts and even bouts of derisive laughter . It quickly became clear this is not an audience in the mood to negotiate or even contemplate changes to the community they have enjoyed , many for decades . And they don&amp;rsquo ; t trust the assurances they were getting from the developers&amp;rsquo ; hired guns . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The entire evening felt as it had been heavily stage-managed to at least create the appearance of community consultation without actually answering public concerns or adapting plans on the basis of legitimate public input . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Residents voiced worries about everything from traffic chaos to storm water management and , of course , the Mother-of-All worries &amp;mdash ; the impact on property values for existing homeowners . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Local councillor Jenna Sudds summed up the session by conceding it was a difficult community conversation , but remained confident that residents can win the fight in the courts . We&amp;rsquo ; ll know soon enough . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The city has sought an expedited court ruling on whether a 38-year-old legal agreement actually binds the property owner ( ClubLink ) to retain the golf course lands as green-space in perpetuity . In other words , can it really be expected that a legal agreement signed nearly four decades ago by two entities ( Campeau Corp . and City of Kanata ) that don&amp;rsquo ; t even exist today be expected to last forever . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The local association representing homeowners has employed its own planning expert who argues the agreement is binding and furthermore makes the case that the development proposal fails to conform to the city&amp;rsquo ; s Official Plan or the Planning Act . Arguments for another day , for sure . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Meantime , Sudds assured residents that the development was far from a done deal and was &amp;ldquo ; only a planning proposal at this point . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But you sensed deep worries setting in among many homeowners about whether it was already too late to successfully push back against well-funded developers who appear to have had their plans in the works for months , maybe years , and who are highly experienced in these kind of public spats. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Not surprisingly , the community is upset , on edge , &amp;rdquo ; Sudds said in a brief interview following the session . She believes the community is 100% opposed to the development plan and isn&amp;rsquo ; t interested in concessions to placate them . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A prominent lobbyist with ties to the provincial Conservatives was seen lurking in the corridors during the sessions , likely on behalf of the developers . That may be significant . The issue could end up before the province&amp;rsquo ; s quasi-judicial Local Planning Appeal Board , which replaced the OMB last year and acts as a tribunal to hear appeals from the development industry . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Come to think if it , where was Dr. Merilee Fullerton , the local Conservative MPP ? You would think she&amp;rsquo ; d play a starring role in this battle , even if only symbolically , by standing behind residents , given that it will affect hundreds of her constituents . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For his part , Watson said yesterday the city remains strongly behind residents in the fight over golf course development . It&amp;rsquo ; s not entirely clear that feeling will be unanimously shared if it ever comes to full city council for debate . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Some inner city councillors may not have much stomach for a fight to preserve the elitist lifestyle of well-moneyed golf enthusiasts . That&amp;rsquo ; s isn&amp;rsquo ; t the reality , but the perception is there for some to exploit . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Besides , the city didn&amp;rsquo ; t exactly rally behind the low-income residents of Herongate last year when a developer evicted hundreds of residents and demolished dozens from their homes to build more expensive units . Apples and oranges perhaps , except in the world of politics , appearances are everything . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Gibbons is a veteran journalist/broadcaster &lt;/em&gt; &lt;em&gt;and former publisher and chief executive of the Ottawa Sun&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Email : &lt;a href= " **31;35276;TOOLONG " **49;35309;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " http : **34;35360;TOOLONG ... Ottawa talks a good game on homelessness , but really has n't done much about ithttp : **38;35513;TOOLONG ... src= " https : **34;35553;TOOLONG ... title= " After two rooming home fires in the area there are a group of people who can not find an affordable place to call home , so have built a tent commune in a wooded area behind the Bayview Station . " alt= " After two rooming home fires in the area there are a group of people who can not find an affordable place to call home , so have built a tent commune in a wooded area behind the Bayview Station . " data-portal-copyright= " Ashley Fraser " **28;35589;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 537818 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; A recent public opinion poll claims homelessness is the top priority of Ottawans . Yet more than halfway through an ambitious 10-year strategy to eliminate the scourge of chronic homelessness in Ottawa , the situation is getting far worse , not better , &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; You don&amp;rsquo ; t see residents flooding city hall with complaints over that failure the way they do over potholes or ugly expansions to the Ch&amp;acirc ; teau Laurier . If they did , we might start to see real progress in resolving a crisis that , right now , is nothing less than a disgrace . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Since the ambitious city-wide strategy of eliminating chronic homelessness was launched in 2014 , the number of people forced into emergency shelters has actually grown nearly 22 per cent , according to figures released last week by the Alliance to End Homelessness . This is not what success on the homeless front was supposed to look like and it certainly doesn&amp;rsquo ; t suggest Ottawans are sufficiently seized with the issue . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The most recent tangible evidence of the city&amp;rsquo ; s housing crunch comes by way of an impromptu tent city that has sprung up near the Bayview LRT station of late , housing nearly a dozen people left homeless by a rooming house fire . They had nowhere to go because the shelters are full . But you can also see it every day in the number of people looking for handouts at intersections or who live on the streets in our inner city . None of that has eased since a declaration was made to end chronic homelessness by 2024. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Meanwhile , the waiting list for social housing jumped nearly 15 per cent last year to an all-time high of 12,163 applicants , despite city investments to increase the supply of affordable and supportive housing . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This is especially worrying since those who can&amp;rsquo ; t afford a roof over their heads are often just a pay cheque or two away from being on the streets themselves . This is where the city can make significant inroads into the homeless crisis by easing the problem before it happens . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The latest city budget calls for another $15 million to be invested in affordable housing and to address the homeless issue . But it&amp;rsquo ; s unlikely to have a dramatic impact on addressing the crisis any more than previous relatively modest investments . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That&amp;rsquo ; s not to suggest the money isn&amp;rsquo ; t needed . It is &amp;mdash ; desperately . But right now , the city seems to be in a holding pattern of trying to keep the number of homeless from growing without ever achieving the once lofty target of eliminating chronic homelessness entirely . Good intentions and ambitious goal-setting simply aren&amp;rsquo ; t enough . We need to declare a war on homelessness and bring all the resources necessary to bear to win it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;35619;TOOLONG ... title= " A man starts a little fire in a camp stove he is able to charge batteries and heat with . He has a budget of $1200-$1300 a month to spend on an apartment for his fianc ? and infant daughter , who are not living with him currently in the tent , but is unable to secure a spot due to shortages of available apartments in the city . Fraser " **28;35655;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 542875 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The current battle plan includes a so-called &amp;ldquo ; Housing First&amp;rdquo ; strategy aimed at getting chronically homeless off the streets and out of shelters into first-stage supportive housing where they can receive counselling and begin a path back to self sufficiency . It&amp;rsquo ; s an excellent plan that broke with the traditional notion of simply warehousing homeless in temporary emergency shelters . But there is a desperate shortage of first stage housing to support the strategy and , after four years of trying , it&amp;rsquo ; s having very limited results . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; According to the alliance , the strategy was supposed to have reduced the number of chronically homeless by 500 a year , yet in the last four years only 225 people have graduated from the program . It&amp;rsquo ; s a depressing result given the magnitude of the problem . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The recent city budget will help , but the city can&amp;rsquo ; t do it alone . Peter Tilley of the Ottawa Mission says the latest $15 million investment is welcome , but still far short of what&amp;rsquo ; s needed to address the gravity of the current crisis . He urges the province and federal government to help cities cope . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Maybe it was a mistake to declare a 10-year strategy to eliminate chronic homelessness as it may have left the impression among many citizens that the matter was well in hand and on the road to being fixed . It also signalled that a solution actually existed , even though it remains one of the most vexing challenges that cities face across the country . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There&amp;rsquo ; s also another misperception out there &amp;mdash ; that a hot economy , with low unemployment , will drastically improve the homeless situation as more people get jobs . Yet a hot economy is actually making things worse as an already tight market for affordable housing grows even tighter amid a housing boom . And that&amp;rsquo ; s hitting families especially hard . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; We need a new plan , more partners and a much bigger resolve to fight homelessness if we are to end it once and for all . That&amp;rsquo ; s when we&amp;rsquo ; ll know it&amp;rsquo ; s a top priority . " data-portal-copyright= " Tony Caldwell " **28;35985;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 541054 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; There&amp;rsquo ; s no disputing we face a transit crisis , but surely the city is overreacting with a plan to add yet more buses into the struggling system , this time a 20-vehicle super-fleet of emergency buses that will stand by , engines running , ready to swoop into action whenever the LRT breaks down , come the New Year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; If the city keeps responding to the LRT mess with ever-grander solutions like this , there may be bigger things to worry about than late trains or overstuffed buses . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The city has already heaped millions of dollars in unplanned expenses onto the desk of RTG/RTM , the private consortium that&amp;rsquo ; s contracted to maintain LRT for the next 30 years . And it plans to heap millions more to cover off this latest plan . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Add to that , the $60 million the city has already withheld from RTG as compensation for those 18 months of delays in launching the LRT and you start to get a picture of a partnership that&amp;rsquo ; s in rough financial shape . So much so that it&amp;rsquo ; s starting to raise real worries about just how much the city is protected in the contractual partnership with RTG. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; More on that in a minute . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The latest addition of another 20 buses to the city&amp;rsquo ; s emergency transit strategy will eventually bring the total to nearly 60 the number added to the system just since LRT launched in September . Remember , LRT was supposed to result in fewer buses and fewer drivers , not more . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The latest plan was unveiled at a Transit Commission meeting yesterday where the city was , at the same time , providing assurances of big progress in improving LRT service . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Apparently , the LRT has been operating virtually trouble free of late , save for another idiot who tried to pry open the train doors on Wednesday . Well , you can&amp;rsquo ; t fix stupid , but you can improve on the number of mechanical failures as well as the time it takes to fix them and , according to transit chair Allan Hubley , big progress was being made on both fronts . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So , that&amp;rsquo ; s the good news . But if things are improving , do we really need an emergency fleet of 20 more buses and drivers that will spend most of the time in the parking lot of the unused Coventry Road baseball park , engines running , waiting for the call to spring into action if the LRT breaks down during peak hours ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;36015;TOOLONG ... title= " City of Ottawa Transit Commission member Coun. " data-portal-copyright= " Errol McGihon " **28;36051;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 541687 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Apparently we do need them , at least so long as somebody else is expected to pay for them . And that could become the source of a much bigger problem down the road . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The city plans to add the cost to a running tab of millions in cost overruns already incurred since the launch of LRT and already being deducted from the monthly charges paid to RTG for maintaining the LRT. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So far , there&amp;rsquo ; s no indication either way that RTG agrees that it&amp;rsquo ; s responsible for all these additional charges . It&amp;rsquo ; s one thing to assume costs directly attributable to fixing trains , but adding the cost of 80 more buses plus millions in other charges , without an absolutely clear understanding by both parties about who is paying for them , seems to be a recipe for a giant lawsuit down the road . One that could take years to resolve . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the meantime , RTG is facing a growing mountain of unpaid bills from private construction companies that want to get paid for their work on LRT. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; RTG is on the entirely hook for all of those unpaid invoices . However , it adds to a picture of financial stress for a company the city is counting on to keep its trains running on time for the next 30 years . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; On Wednesday , city manager Steve Kanellakos assured councillors they need not worry about the city&amp;rsquo ; s being vulnerable to any potential bankruptcy by RTG . We should hope he is right . I&amp;rsquo ; m less sure everybody was feeling the warm and fuzzies from that assurance . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; My fear is if RTG/RTM are no longer the service providers , &amp;rdquo ; Coun. There isn&amp;rsquo ; t exactly a standing list of other companies ready and able to step in to manage a maintenance contract as complex as the LRT , and the city is simply not tooled to do it itself . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So , could the city be forced to shutdown the LRT if the maintenance agreement collapsed ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s possible , &amp;rdquo ; Brockington said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Gulp ! &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Now there&amp;rsquo ; s a nightmare scenario . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Gibbons is a veteran journalist/broadcaster and former publisher and chief executive of the Ottawa Sun . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **31;36081;TOOLONG " **38;36114;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;36154;TOOLONG ... Buses the LRT solution and other things learned at city hall&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; Rick GibbonsThu , 21 Nov 2019 10:35:28 **45;36259;TOOLONG ... LRT fiasco weighs heavily on Watson 's political futurehttp : **34;36306;TOOLONG ... src= " https : **34;36342;TOOLONG ... title= " HAPPIER TIMES : Jim Watson enjoys the first LRT ride during the LRT launch , September 14 , 2019. " alt= " HAPPIER TIMES : Jim Watson enjoys the first LRT ride during the LRT launch , September 14 , 2019. " data-portal-copyright= " Jean Levac " **28;36378;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 530730 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; LRT is supposed to be the crowning achievement of Mayor Jim Watson&amp;rsquo ; s career at city hall and may still be , assuming the current transit fiasco is resolved reasonably soon . But with each passing day of LRT disruptions , there is perhaps an equal chance emerging that transit ends up being Watson&amp;rsquo ; s one-way ticket out of office in three years&amp;rsquo ; time , a seemingly impossible thought just a few months ago . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Right now , LRT is slipping into a deep crisis and may cost millions of dollars to manage before things stabilize . Yes , it&amp;rsquo ; s becoming just that serious that a mayor who has never faced significant political opposition in his career may be vulnerable like never before . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Since retaking the mayor&amp;rsquo ; s chair in 2010 , Watson has enjoyed an unassailable grip on city council affairs , so much so that councillors were once accused of being little more than bobble-heads , given their seeming enthusiasm to support just about anything he tossed onto the council table . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; From the outset , he brought discipline to a chaotic budgeting process under his predecessor , Larry O&amp;rsquo ; Brien , and made it clear who was in charge at city hall . He pointed to redevelopment of Lansdowne as real progress under his leadership . A few pretenders would emerge in election years , but he faced no serious challenge for the job since taking it on . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He knew how to work the corridors , twisting councillor arms when necessary , doling out goodies when he could to keep councillors onside. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When not conducting official city hall duties , Watson is usually found at bake sales or store openings ; no local event is too small , so long as it allows him to connect with local residents and hear what&amp;rsquo ; s important to them . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He has been as popular a politician as you&amp;rsquo ; re going to find anywhere , yet those days may be slipping away little by little as tens of thousands of weary commuters brave icy cold winds , crowded platforms and long delays in getting to work and home again . They&amp;rsquo ; re looking for somebody to blame and Mr. Nice Guy is starting to feel the brunt of it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Watson&amp;rsquo ; s also getting a much chillier reception at city hall these days where a number of councillors are standing up to him , often publicly . An alliance of inner city , left-of-centre councillors has begun to push back hard over LRT failures and other issues like bike road safety and the lack of affordable housing . They see Watson as vulnerable and will likely seize on that during the approaching budget debate . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Rookie Coun. Shawn Menard , in particular , seems to delight in poking Watson in the ribs at every opportunity . Even fellow rookie Carol Anne Meehan has begun to emerge as a Watson critic , or at least refuses to be part of what she sees as an inner circle of council favourites . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Whether or not the current transit crisis is resolved soon , LRT will remain front and centre for the balance this council&amp;rsquo ; s term as councillors cast a much more critical eye in monitoring progress of Phase Two , fearing a repeat of the current nightmare . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; If that happens then Watson will be really under the gun by next election and may even decide to leave . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I suspect there are three possible contenders for the mayor&amp;rsquo ; s job next term , two of whom might be ready to tackle Watson head on and a third who may be attracted into the race only if Watson steps aside , which is a real possibility . Watson has never lost an election in his political life and has no intention of ever doing so . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; If he does hang around for another election , he could face a strong challenge on the left from Menard while current senator and former Ottawa police chief Vern White could challenge from the centre-right of the political spectrum . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Each needs the other to enter the race in order to weaken Watson&amp;rsquo ; s broad support and thereby increase his own chances . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Who is the third possible candidate ? Carol Anne Meehan. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A clearer picture will start to emerge in a year when this current council passes the half way mark . That&amp;rsquo ; s likely when Watson will survey the field of possible contenders , reflect on his own legacy and decide whether he can safely take another run or hang up his ceremonial chain of office . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I&amp;rsquo ; m betting his decision hangs on the success of LRT and right now that train&amp;rsquo ; s having trouble leaving the station . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Gibbons is a veteran journalist and broadcaster and former publisher and chief executive of the Ottawa Sun . &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **31;36408;TOOLONG " **38;36441;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;36481;TOOLONG ... Let 's not lose our sense of humour amid the LRT problemshttp : **32;36633;TOOLONG ... src= " https : **34;36667;TOOLONG ... title= " Jim Watson enjoys the first LRT ride during the LRT launch , September 14 , 2019. " data-portal-copyright= " Jean Levac " **28;36703;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 540051 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; A rabbi , a Buddhist monk and a priest exit a stalled train and the rabbi says &amp;hellip ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Wait ! I take it back . I get it . No joking about LRT . Don&amp;rsquo ; t want to be thrown under the proverbial transit bus for the crime of showing even a hint of levity during Ottawa&amp;rsquo ; s winter transit crunch . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Mayor Jim Watson learned that lesson the hard way this week when he approached a microphone and joked to a room of tourism folks that he was sorry he was late &amp;ldquo ; because I was waiting for the LRT. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Good line delivered before the perfect audience . He got a pretty good laugh for it too until the Twittersphere got wind of it , whereupon various humourless nitwits promptly demanded his resignation or worse for the crime of showing a little humour amid the rancour over terrible transit service since the LRT launched . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It was disappointing for sure &amp;mdash ; not that he made the joke , but that he felt compelled to apologize the next day , thereby further cementing the city&amp;rsquo ; s tired reputation as the Town that Fun Completely Forgot . Or maybe critics were just trying to chalk up another prized catch in a culture in which everyone is offended by just about everything these days . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s perfectly fine to hold Watson and all city councillors to account for LRT problems , but let&amp;rsquo ; s not go overboard . These are First World problems , even if those overstuffed buses and trains look a little Third Worldly of late . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; These ( remarks ) were not intended to minimize the significant challenges that commuters have faced since the launch of LRT , &amp;rdquo ; a chastened Watson tweeted yesterday . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Of course they weren&amp;rsquo ; t , and he shouldn&amp;rsquo ; t have had to explain it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He even said the comments were &amp;ldquo ; self-deprecating. &amp;rdquo ; In other words , the joke was really on him because he owns ultimate responsibility for the LRT . He&amp;rsquo ; s not running away from that . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But by offering a little one-liner , he showed he was not going to get caught up in the hysteria that has gripped much of the debate over fixing transit in this city either . Good for him . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Does anybody seriously think Watson isn&amp;rsquo ; t losing sleep over the transit mess ? Still , it&amp;rsquo ; s astonishing to see how even some councillors who merrily approved the new transit system at each juncture now stand back in horror and point fingers at others . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Let&amp;rsquo ; s all take a deep breath and recognize it&amp;rsquo ; s a complex system that didn&amp;rsquo ; t roll out very well and there will be lots of problems before they are fixed . The point is they&amp;rsquo ; re fixable. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It may take time and more money than budgeted to get things in shape , but it will happen eventually . The only thing we can try to do in the meantime is mitigate the inconvenience and not lose our sanity or civility in the process . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s good that the city is open to suggestions , but let&amp;rsquo ; s just not get carried away with crazy ideas like shutting the entire system down and reverting to the old network of buses until the thing is fixed . That makes no sense because things just aren&amp;rsquo ; t that bad . Besides , Ottawans need to work the system hard for deficiencies to be identified . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The transit commission meets next week and the first point of order should be to reintroduce the parallel bus service that operated during the first weeks of LRT launch . That much is a given . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Maybe they should also revisit the 30-year maintenance agreement the city signed with RTG . If the consortium can&amp;rsquo ; t meet its end of the bargain , perhaps the city should sue RTG , revoke the contract and find a service provider more responsive to problems and more capable of making things work . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Finally , maybe they should revisit the rollout strategy for Phase 2 . Rather than build and roll out the entire LRT extension at once , why not consider a phased approach ? In other words , hurry up construction timelines on a few new stations and use them to spread out bus arrivals and departures where commuters connect with the LRT and thereby minimize the kind of choke-point problems associated with dropping everybody off at Blair and Tunney&amp;rsquo ; s Pasture . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Meantime , let&amp;rsquo ; s all accept this has been a season of hell for commuters . We don&amp;rsquo ; t need to lose our sense of humour while doing so . It might be the only way to keep our sanity . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;hellip ; and the rabbi says to his colleagues , &amp;ldquo ; there&amp;rsquo ; s an escalator ahead , the largest in Canada , with many steps . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; A path to enlightenment , &amp;rdquo ; says the monk . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; A veritable stairway to heaven , &amp;rdquo ; adds the priest . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The three board the escalator , which breaks down immediately , forcing them onto a crowded 400-step stairway . Exhausted , they call an Uber . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Serenity now , &amp;rdquo ; the monk mutters as they disappear into the night . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Serenity now . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Gibbons is a veteran journalist and broadcaster and former publisher and chief executive of the Ottawa Sun &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **31;36733;TOOLONG " **59;36766;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; Rick GibbonsFri , 15 Nov 2019 11:00:04 **45;36827;TOOLONG ... I noticed it at the time and surmised she simply preferred to stand while she worked rather than slump into a chair for a couple of hours . Turned out she was taking a stand &amp;mdash ; literally &amp;mdash ; by refusing to sit at the same council table as Chiarelli , who sat expressionless several seats to her left . Chiarelli faces numerous but so far unproven allegations of misconduct from more than a dozen women who previously worked in his office . &amp;ldquo ; I always tell women how important it is to take their seat at the table , &amp;lsquo ; &amp;rsquo ; Sudds tweeted afterward. &amp;ldquo ; However , today felt like a day I just couldn&amp;rsquo ; t sit at the table . Right now , Coun. &lt;strong&gt;Diane Deans&lt;/strong&gt; ( Gloucester-Southgate ) is absent while she takes care of some serious medical issues . Coun. &lt;strong&gt;Tobi Nussbaum&lt;/strong&gt; announced he was vacating his Rideau-Rockcliffe seat just two months after being re-elected in 2018 to take a new job as CEO of the NCC . Could this become a model to resolve the future of the Kanata Lakes Golf Course ? Right now , it&amp;rsquo ; s on a very different path with a legal challenge heading to the courts . I suspect Sudds , who is leading the community fight to retain the green space , is following the Stonebridge case closely . Or she should be . &amp;hellip ; Ditto Coun. &lt;strong&gt;Glen Gower&lt;/strong&gt; who is managing his own golf course issue in his Stittsville ward . Gower says the course is not at risk of development , in part because it&amp;rsquo ; s built on a floodplain . With development off the table , there are big concerns about how the community will get itself out of a financial hole . One possible solution is fundraising , but if it fails the community may have little choice but to suck it up and propose a special levy on homeowners . Thousands of people on other islands were not . Many of those rebuilding rely on the pig business . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So Todd&amp;rsquo ; s book is helping . Recently , the Ottawa screening of his documentary at 50 Sussex helped raise $23,000 . Many businesses donated resources , from the venue to the food . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It all started decades ago , when a small island in Exuma , known as Staniel Cay , had a problem . With the tourism industry growing , the pigs had become a nuisance . They smelled and sometimes escaped their pens . So they were moved to an uninhabited island . They taught themselves to swim to greet those who cared for them . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; What started as a farm changed over time . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Today , tourists head to the beach to see how the pigs have adapted to their island retreat . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; When we launched our campaign to bring these animals to the world , I thought it would be popular . I had no idea the swimming pigs would become the global sensation they are today . There are now nine pig colonies in The Bahamas . Millions of people see them each year . It contributes millions to the country&amp;rsquo ; s economy , &amp;rdquo ; he says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Todd partnered with well-known Ottawa business leader Peter Nicholson , the president and founder of the foundation WCPD , a financial services firm specializing in philanthropy . Using the tax code , the company assists large donors in giving more to charity . Since 2006 , it has generated more than $125 million in donations for its clients across Canada . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Nicholson , who is also the largest owner of Grand Isle Resort in Exuma , was looking for a way to bring more attention to the area . That was when Todd suggested a marketing campaign about the pigs . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; In many respects , that image of the pigs swimming in crystal-clear water has become a symbol of The Bahamas itself , &amp;rdquo ; Todd says . &amp;ldquo ; The swimming pig is the country&amp;rsquo ; s Mickey Mouse . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At the documentary screening , The Bahamas High Commissioner to Canada Alvin Smith spoke about what the country needs . Fundraising is one part . The second part is tourism . Many people believe all of the islands were damaged . They weren&amp;rsquo ; t . On the day of the hurricane , it was sunny on the pigs&amp;rsquo ; island , which is 300 km away from the devastation . Grand Isle Resort was completely untouched . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Peter and I felt we had to do something here in Ottawa . The Bahamas has been a huge part of my life for about 10 years now . And for Peter , he has been investing in the country for more than 14 years . The Bahamas is our adopted home . Many Bahamians are our friends . Hurricane Dorian was unprecedented . The Bahamas has been hit by hurricanes before . This storm was especially ruthless , &amp;rdquo ; he says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And this week , Todd released his fourth book . The Sandbox Diary is fiction and based on his Middle East experiences , specifically in the United Arab Emirates . That was where he helped launch the country&amp;rsquo ; s largest English language newspaper . While satire , it delves into some serious issues , like the clash between so-called &amp;ldquo ; western culture&amp;rdquo ; and the more conservative Islamic state . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Philanthropy is second nature for both Todd and Nicholson . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In addition to the work done by WCPD they are the founders of the Exuma Marathon , taking place this Saturday . The race , now entering its 5th year , promotes tourism and provides a scholarship to one student on the island each year , so he or she can attend university . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And in the spirit of philanthropy , on Nov. 13 , WCPD will once again serve as the presenting sponsor of the Ottawa Philanthropy Awards . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The pigs will be pleased . &lt;/p&gt; Kimothy WalkerFri , 08 Nov 2019 22:07:57 **45;37330;TOOLONG ... Rick Chiarelli will slip through a side door , possibly this Wednesday , more likely though at the last council meeting of the month , Nov. 27 . " data-portal-copyright= " Julie Oliver " **28;38102;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 536846 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Jesus , take the wheel ! In less than two months , LRT has gone from fancy red-carpet rollout to runaway train . How bad is it ? Conductor-in-Chief Jim Watson , who was accused of being asleep at the switch of late and who routinely asks commuters for a little patience , please , is now throwing caution to the wind along with another $3.5 million to get transit back on track . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I guess another few million is small beans in a multi-billion-dollar transit service that just can&amp;rsquo ; t seem to run on time , but that&amp;rsquo ; s not the real price being paid for what may have been a hurried launch of the new rail system , as some suspect . That price is being paid daily by commuters frustrated by endless delays and sick of all the excuses and false assurances that have accompanied them . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; People don&amp;rsquo ; t want excuses . They just want to get to work and home again without the daily commute turning into a messy , unpredictable triathlon of buses , trains and unscheduled hikes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Just wait until Wednesday when city council meets and when the transit commissioners gather for the first time in nearly two months to do a post mortem on a pretty miserable roll-out of their best-laid plans . Surely somebody&amp;rsquo ; s going to get pinned for this mess . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;38132;TOOLONG ... title= " A lineup of commuters at the Tunney 's Pasture LRT station . " alt= " A lineup of commuters at the Tunney 's Pasture LRT station . " data-portal-copyright= " Julie Oliver " **28;38168;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 536846 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; There&amp;rsquo ; ll be no shortage of testy questions about exactly what happened during that final 12-day testing phase of LRT . Did somebody move the goal posts to ensure the service launched successfully on a prescribed date so as not to mess with launch celebrations ? You&amp;rsquo ; ll hear that question a lot . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; All it took was another miserable day of commuter frustration Friday for Watson to finally express what commuters have been shouting for weeks . They&amp;rsquo ; re furious and , like Howard Beale , the frustrated TV anchor in the movie classic Network , Watson finally opened his metaphorical Twitter window to scream that he was sick of the problems , too , and wasn&amp;rsquo ; t going to take it any more ! &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; To say I am furious with the poor performance of our LRT system is an understatement , &amp;rdquo ; Watson fumed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I swear I heard commuters shouting in unison : &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s about time ! &amp;rdquo ; Yes , commuters aren&amp;rsquo ; t going to take it any more , for sure . They&amp;rsquo ; re tired of being left stranded at bus stops or on over-crowded train platforms . They&amp;rsquo ; re sick of stuck doors , faulty switches , jammed buses and trains and a thousand other glitches in the system that has left many Ottawans wondering exactly what they&amp;rsquo ; ve bought into . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Over the last few weeks , we have been as frustrated as our transit users with the poor performance of LRT and the unreliability of our bus system , &amp;rdquo ; Watson said in announcing a trainload of interim measures , including 40 more buses deployed into the transit system and in excess of a dozen more in the new year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So , that&amp;rsquo ; s the solution ? Adding dozens more buses to a service that was supposed to need many fewer buses with the launch of LRT ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; More buses means many more bus drivers hitting the roads and , no doubt , landing on the province&amp;rsquo ; s notorious annual Sunshine List of public employees earning in excess of $100,000 a year . Christmas just came early for them . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; According to Watson , further measures will be announced when the transit budget is discussed next week . Can&amp;rsquo ; t wait . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the meantime , Watson warned the consortium will pay dearly for delivering a substandard LRT . To do that , the city will begin deducting $2.8 million from the monthly payments to RTG until the system is performing to an acceptable standard . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Taxpayers can be forgiven if they feel their standing on the wrong side of the tracks as trains zoom by . Costs are going up and presumably ticket revenues are going down as frustrated commuters look for alternatives . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Meantime , winter is coming fast and the prospect of these problems persisting into frigid temperatures , ice and heavy snow is enough to make you pine for the old days of OC Transpo service or maybe wondering if dog sled or snow shoes might be more viable options . " data-portal-copyright= " Errol McGihon " **28;39046;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 530517 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Kanata residents will meet Monday night for an update on the proposed Kanata Golf and Country Club redevelopment and you can bet a clubhouse beer the city will be taking note of attendance . Ditto the developers , who also want to gauge just how deep community opposition really is to the controversial development plan now that local residents have had time to digest some of the details . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Even if you don&amp;rsquo ; t golf or live anywhere near the plush rolling grounds of the Kanata Lakes course , you might want to keep tabs on how this all unfolds over the next year or so . That&amp;rsquo ; s because it just might answer a question or two that have been rolling around city hall for some time now : Do developers wield too much power in Ottawa ? And do citizens or even the city really have any business dictating what private property owners do , provided it&amp;rsquo ; s generally in keeping with the surrounding land use . Remember the Ch&amp;acirc ; teau Laurier brouhaha ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s been a month since Minto and Richcraft released their vision for the community and they are hoping its colourful pamphlets and lofty promises of maintaining existing tree stands and creating &amp;ldquo ; parkettes&amp;rdquo ; have eased at least some of the initial community backlash. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The city is probably looking for the same answer . Truth is , the city has better things to do than engage in an expensive and protracted legal battle with high-profile developers . It also stands to earn the benefit of new taxes derived from all those new homes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But , at least for now , the city is fully onside with residents . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Kanata North Coun. Jenna Sudds is determined to keep it that way . On Friday , she informed residents that the city is seeking an expedited court order to force ClubLink to honour a development agreement signed by a previous course owner back when Kanata was a fast-expanding city in its own right , prior to amalgamation. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I share everyone&amp;rsquo ; s frustration that we must deal with this application that has a total disregard for our community and legal agreements , &amp;rdquo ; she assured her constituents . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; From the outset , that agreement bound the owner of the club &amp;mdash ; who ever it was &amp;mdash ; to retain the property forever as a golf course , or at least parkland , as part of a broader guarantee that 40 per cent of the Kanata Lakes community would be retained as green space . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Hundreds of homeowners whose homes back onto the course or are nearby , have a lot riding on the outcome as it could impact the value of their property investments . They paid premiums to live on or near a course and fear their future land values would be eroded sharply if the golf course is replaced by town homes or other development . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The so-called 40 per cent rule lies at the heart of this new battle and a legal decision could ultimately set precedent for any similar agreements elsewhere . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; If the city ultimately wins in court , ClubLink will be ordered to either withdraw the development application it has filed with the city or hand ownership of the lands over to the city at no cost . But there&amp;rsquo ; s plenty of wiggle room for appeals that could tie up this fight for years . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I suspect there&amp;rsquo ; s a greater chance of me beating Kim Jong Un on the golf course ( he scored five holes-in-one in his first game ) than ClubLink waving a course flag in surrender and forking over a valuable piece of real estate for free . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So what&amp;rsquo ; s the alternative ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Given the value of land at stake , I&amp;rsquo ; m surprised ClubLink hasn&amp;rsquo ; t made a few generous overtures to the community to at least try to lessen public opposition , perhaps by offering to shell out for an arena , a community centre or some other community-owned space or facility . It might make the deal a little more attractive for some residents . Heck , it could offer free memberships at its other golf courses in the region for those most affected . I&amp;rsquo ; m sure that would placate many club members . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Surely , the developers , who have a lot at stake in this battle , can pony up a few ideas of their own to placate existing homeowners . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Maybe even the city could chime in with details on how property taxes could be lowered to reflect the reduced value of some properties . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The alternative , of course , is to batten down the hatches and take to the bunkers in preparation for a long and very expensive legal battle ahead . Right now , it&amp;rsquo ; s get ready for war . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Gibbons is a veteran journalist/broadcaster and former publisher and chief executive of the Ottawa Sun . &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **31;39076;TOOLONG " **38;39109;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;39149;TOOLONG ... A little inspiration on how to live your best lifehttp : **36;39301;TOOLONG ... src= " https : **34;39339;TOOLONG ... title= " In her early twenties , Lindsay Campbell had one ovary removed because of signs of cancer . " data-portal-copyright= " Julie Oliver " **28;39375;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 534263 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s not every day that an unborn baby saves a life , but that is exactly what happened to Lindsay Campbell in her 20s . Her story is about survival . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Campbell was pregnant with her second child when doctors discovered a cancerous tumour on her ovary . She had already had one ovary removed years earlier that showed early signs of cancer . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Ultrasounds from my pregnancy resulted in the second growth being discovered , &amp;rdquo ; she says . &amp;ldquo ; I &amp;hellip ; had my last remaining ovary and tube removed with ( my daughter&amp;rsquo ; s ) birth . I experienced physical and emotional pain , many surgeries over a fairly short amount of time and the devastation of infertility and a surgically induced menopause at 28 years old . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ovarian cancer is very difficult to detect until it&amp;rsquo ; s often too late . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; What kept me going was the strength of other women going through ovarian cancer , chemotherapy and radiation , the women who found out too late and their families struggling to cope with the loss of their mother , sister or friend , &amp;rdquo ; she adds . &amp;ldquo ; My children kept me going , too . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The process and trauma caused her weight to soar to 350 pounds . In a herculean effort , she changed her entire life . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She was enduring depression and had to use a cane as she developed plantar fasciitis , an inflammation of the tissue that connects your toes to your heel . ( I&amp;rsquo ; ve had it . It hurts &amp;mdash ; a lot. ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Yet Campbell , a new single mother , set about to change . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; My first piece of advice is to make a list of everything that is holding you back . What do you have zero control over ? Acknowledge it , feel it , cry and scream about it if you need to &amp;mdash ; then let it go . What can you change ? Make a plan and execute it , &amp;rdquo ; she says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; First , she started working on weight loss . She&amp;rsquo ; s not sure she was 350 pounds because her home scale didn&amp;rsquo ; t go that high . That&amp;rsquo ; s the last number a doctor provided to her . Now she&amp;rsquo ; s almost half that . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I joined an amazing local combat sports gym where my kids took muay Thai and Brazilian jiu-jitsu classes while I did high-intensity fitness classes on the same mats , at the same time , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &amp;ldquo ; I met an incredible trainer who pushed me to reach my goal of getting stronger and getting me off of my cane with the help of a great physiotherapist . This summer , I ran my first Spartan race . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Campbell works out six days a week . Next on her list was her career , which was going nowhere fast . So , she quit her job &amp;mdash ; yes , just like that . She enrolled in school and will graduate in 2020 from Algonquin College with a business administration diploma . The online format allowed her to be home with her kids . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; My last piece of advice is to put yourself first . It&amp;rsquo ; s not selfish , &amp;rdquo ; she says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; You will find out very quickly that when you begin to make yourself a priority , you glow . People notice and you begin to attract good things and good people . Your children , friends and family see a happy person and that happiness spreads . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This column space was intended , years ago , to be about people doing extraordinary things in our community and sometimes the inspiration starts at home . When a friend introduced me to Campbell as &amp;ldquo ; someone you need to meet , &amp;rdquo ; I thought if Campbell can turn her life around , can&amp;rsquo ; t others ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I am working toward starting my own business that integrates my love for health and fitness . I want to help and inspire others to achieve their goals , &amp;rdquo ; Campbell says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; So many people think they are stuck and that they can&amp;rsquo ; t change their situation because of barriers they&amp;rsquo ; re facing . I want to help people by acknowledging these barriers , working with them to knock down the barriers , so they can be their best self . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;39405;TOOLONG ... bills going up despite Ford election promise&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;39440;TOOLONG ... " data-portal-copyright= " James Park " **28;39630;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 533884 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Cancel the redecorators . Deflate the blue party balloons . The Liberals&amp;rsquo ; vaunted election machine painted the town Liberal red again yesterday . They may have lost momentum elsewhere , but not in the nation&amp;rsquo ; s capital . As the great political philosopher Rihanna once opined : &amp;ldquo ; Funny how things could change , but remain the same . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Locally , bureaucrats , no doubt , are breathing easier over the receding prospect of layoffs in their ranks with a Liberal win , even if it is a minority , though truth is the Conservatives never really posed a big threat in that regard . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While tens of thousands of government workers in this burgh continue to be plagued by the Phoenix pay scandal , for whatever reason they decided not to make the Liberals pay for it , perhaps out of fear the Conservatives might make things even worse . Certainly , that&amp;rsquo ; s how the country&amp;rsquo ; s largest federal public service union &amp;ndash ; PSAC &amp;ndash ; saw things &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Liberals went into the election holding seven of eight Ottawa seats , only to emerge from the hard-fought 40-day campaign having lost no ground whatsoever . And that must be a huge disappointment to the Conservatives and NDP , as both parties saw opportunities to pick up seats in the city slip away . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Conservatives targeted several local Liberal seats like Ottawa West-Nepean as winnable , but failed to gain even an inch of new territory . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In fact , the only local loss for the Liberals and win for the Conservatives came in Carleton where Liberal candidate Chris Rodgers mounted a spirited rematch with Pierre Poilievre , but again couldn&amp;rsquo ; t knock out the veteran Conservative MP and former cabinet minister . Poilievre will , no doubt , now return to the House of Commons to be an even bigger thorn in the backside of a chastened Liberal government , which lost its majority . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When it came to local campaigns , turns out the PM didn&amp;rsquo ; t need to lose sleep over the future of his high profile Environment Minister , Catherine McKenna , who easily survived a clash with Conservative candidate Carol Clemenhagen and NDP star candidate Emilie Taman . Alas , Taman , despite a vigorous , well run campaign , finished a distant second in her bid to return the seat once held by the late Paul Dewar to the NDP. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In other Ottawa ridings : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;In Ottawa West-Nepean , rookie Liberal MP Anita Vandenbeld defeated one of the region 's strongest Conservative candidates , veteran cop and community leader Abdul Abdi , who stepped into the race after the nominated Conservative candidate bailed before the campaign began . Nevertheless , this was a seat the Conservatives thought they could win . &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt;In Orl ? ans , David Bertschi ca n't get any respect , regardless of what party he claims to be supporting these days . The former Liberal leadership contender switched to the Conservatives after he was denied the Liberal nomination in the riding last election . Turns out local voters did n't like him any more as a Conservative . Maybe next time he 'll run for the NDP . The contest was easily won by former Liberal MPP Marie-France Lalonde. &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt;In Nepean , voters returned MP Chandra Arya who will , no doubt , now fade back into the Liberal backbenches till the next election . &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt;Ottawa-Vanier proved again to the one of the safest Liberal seats in Canada . Mona Fortier cruised to an easy win over Conservative Joel E Bernard and NDP candidate Stephanie Mercier. &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt;In Kanata-Carleton , Justina McCaffrey just could n't overcome being a dreadful candidate for the Conservatives . She was a no-show at a debate and never veered from her talking points when she did appear . Her past friendship with Alt-right looney-toon Faith Goldy did n't do her any favours , either . Voters in the riding returned Karen McCrimmon to Parliament for the Liberals . &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt;Ottawa South continued its McGuinty love affair , returning David McGuinty , brother of the former Ontario premier , Dalton McGuinty , for another term . McGuinty cruised to an easy win over his nearest rival , Conservative Eli Tannis. &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; Footnote : Former Ottawa Councillor and failed mayoralty candidate Clive Doucet finished a dismal fourth in his attempt to win election in the riding of Cape Breton-Canso . City of Ottawa okay with a Liberal minority , for now&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; Rick GibbonsTue , 22 Oct 2019 03:46:26 **45;39838;TOOLONG ... 2019OttawaGIBBONS : Think local when you 're casting your votehttp : **36;39885;TOOLONG ... src= " https : **34;39923;TOOLONG ... title= " Independents Jane Philpott , left , and Jody Wilson-Raybould vote in the House of Commons on April 9 . " alt= " Independents Jane Philpott , left , and Jody Wilson-Raybould vote in the House of Commons on April 9 . They 're running for re-election as independents , and Rick Gibbons says voters should try to determine their own Jane or Judy when casting ballots for local MPs in Monday 's election . " data-portal-copyright= " Sean Kilpatrick " **28;39959;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 533288 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Restless ? Can&amp;rsquo ; t Sleep ? Don&amp;rsquo ; t know who to vote for Monday ? Relax . Think local . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; If you can&amp;rsquo ; t decide among the national leadership choices on offer , don&amp;rsquo ; t stay home . Consider instead casting your vote on the basis of good community leadership . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In other words , do what most Canadians don&amp;rsquo ; t : Cast your vote for the best candidate in your riding regardless of party affiliation. &amp;nbsp ; It&amp;rsquo ; s not always easy . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Across Ottawa , there are some very good candidates who have tossed their hats into the ring , yet may not be considered by voters who are driven strictly by party ideology or on the basis of national leadership . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This has been an especially cynical national campaign featuring more Gotcha ! moments than healthy debate and it has left many Canadians wishing there were better choices on offer . So , instead of getting caught up in the big headlines over blackface or dual citizenship , simply ask yourself who would best serve your interests and those of your community when the chips are down . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Don&amp;rsquo ; t be swayed simply by incumbency. &amp;nbsp ; Returning MPs enjoy a natural advantage because they are better known . That doesn&amp;rsquo ; t mean they are the best candidate on offer . In Ottawa&amp;rsquo ; s eight ridings , six feature returning MPs . I&amp;rsquo ; d bet three are vulnerable . Or should be . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Still , that doesn&amp;rsquo ; t mean there aren&amp;rsquo ; t some terrific contests in the other ridings too . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In Carleton riding , veteran Conservative Pierre Poilievre faces a second-time battle with Chris Rodgers , a local teacher and church elder who came oh-so close last time . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Poilievre is a huge thorn in the side of the Liberals and a veteran former cabinet minister who will naturally play a prominent role in a Conservative government . It&amp;rsquo ; s not easy knocking off a veteran like Poilievre , who is a skilled debater and excellent retail politician . It will be a tall order for Rodgers to win , maybe too tall . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In Ottawa West-Nepean , Liberal MP Anita Vandenbeld is by no means assured of retaining her seat . She faces a strong candidate in Conservative Abdul Abdi , a veteran cop and community leader . The Conservatives believe they have a real chance of stealing this one . And maybe they should . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In Ottawa Centre , voters face an interesting choice between two well-qualified candidates : Environment Minister Catherine McKenna and lawyer Emilie Taman for the NDP . It&amp;rsquo ; s hard to believe one of Justin Trudeau&amp;rsquo ; s most high profile cabinet ministers could be at risk here . She is. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The voters of Kanata-Carleton face a choice between Liberal MP Karen McCrimmon and a conservative candidate who skipped some debates and performed poorly when she did appear . Justina McCaffrey has been a lousy candidate for the Conservatives . She hasn&amp;rsquo ; t been helped by a past association with gal pal Faith Goldie , an alt-right nuisance . When it comes to principled local leadership , I don&amp;rsquo ; t think voters face a tough choice here . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Why opt for the best local candidate ? Because much of the work of a typical MP has little to do with Question Period . It&amp;rsquo ; s constituency work , helping residents with their family problems or helping citizens navigate through the federal bureaucracy . We should spend more time considering that during campaigns rather than listening to candidates spout party lines that were written for them . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I&amp;rsquo ; d like to think that , even in a party-driven system , there&amp;rsquo ; s still some room for individuality and some space for principles . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Over and over again , I have heard people say they wish they could vote for Jody Wilson-Raybould or Jane Philpott or someone like them . These two high-profile former Liberal cabinet ministers took principled stands regarding the SNC-Lavalin affair and it cost them their careers as cabinet ministers . Both are running as independents this campaign . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Their experience touched a nerve with many Canadians by reminding us of the importance of principles over party or partisanship . I wonder how many other MPs would take similar stands , even at the risk of losing a cabinet job or a secured nomination next election . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Maybe we should have spent this campaign exploring that issue more deeply with all local candidates instead of getting caught up in the latest Gotcha ! moment of the national campaign . If you&amp;rsquo ; re stuck in the ballot booth and can&amp;rsquo ; t decide who do vote for Monday , then ask yourself this question : Who is your Jody ? Your Jane ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Rick Gibbons is a veteran journalist/broadcaster and former Publisher and CEO of the Ottawa Sun . &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **29;39989;TOOLONG : **50;40020;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;40072;TOOLONG ...
